c11_acc_cbse_01_001: Accounting only records what can be measured in money — important isn't enough. Check: can you price it in rupees?
c12_acc_cbse_01_001: Profit-sharing alone isn't partnership — a lender can share profits. Check: mutual agency plus a business carried on?
c11_acc_cbse_01_002: Book-keeping records what happened; accounting explains what it means. Check: recording or analysing?
c12_acc_cbse_01_002: The deed isn't a formality — interest, salaries and goodwill all flow from it. Check: read it before appropriating?
c11_acc_cbse_01_003: Accounting grew regionally, not in a straight line — Pacioli's leap was the universal dual-aspect frame. Check: better or broader?
c12_acc_cbse_01_003: No deed means equal shares — no interest on capital or salary, whatever the ratios. Check: is there a deed?
c11_acc_cbse_01_004: 'Government' isn't one user — tax, RoC/SEBI and labour each want different data. Check: which department, which need?
c12_acc_cbse_01_004: Fixed capital isn't frozen — permanent additions and withdrawals still hit the Capital Account. Check: routine or permanent?
c11_acc_cbse_01_005: Comparable isn't identical — FIFO and weighted average can coexist if each is applied and disclosed. Check: same or steady?
c12_acc_cbse_01_005: Interest on drawings is income to the firm — credit P&L Appropriation. Check: who receives it?
c11_acc_cbse_01_006: Cost accounting asks what it cost; management asks what to do. Check: ascertaining or deciding?
c12_acc_cbse_01_006: Interest on capital is an appropriation, not a charge — debit P&L Appropriation on capital employed. Check: charge or appropriation?
c11_acc_cbse_01_007: Roles, branches and functions differ — the role is what it does for society. Check: which was asked?
c12_acc_cbse_01_007: Don't default to 6.5 months — quarterly beginning draws 7.5. Check: which drawing pattern?
c11_acc_cbse_01_008: Capital is the owner's claim, not a business asset — the cash brought in is the asset. Check: whose claim?
c12_acc_cbse_01_008: Partner salary isn't an expense — owners aren't staff, so debit P&L Appropriation. Check: expense or appropriation?
c11_acc_cbse_01_009: Revenue/expenses come from ordinary operations; gains/losses from incidental events. Check: which source?
c12_acc_cbse_01_009: A guarantee redistributes the same profit — the shortfall hits the guaranteeing partners' shares. Check: bigger or same pot?
c11_acc_cbse_01_010: Cash leaving isn't always expense — the owner's withdrawal is Drawings. Check: business cost or owner claim?
c12_acc_cbse_01_010: Past-period fixes don't go through this year's P&L — use a P&L Adjustment Account. Check: which year's profit?
c11_acc_cbse_01_011: An owner's withdrawal shrinks Capital, not Liabilities. Check: whose claim reduced?
c12_acc_cbse_01_011: Fixed capital still takes permanent additions and withdrawals — only routine items bypass it. Check: routine or permanent?
c11_acc_cbse_01_012: Limits don't mean unreliable — profit measures what it measures; it just skips morale. Check: what's out of scope?
c12_acc_cbse_02_001: Sacrificing ratio equals old ratio only by default — check how the new partner takes the share. Check: equal or unequal?
c11_acc_cbse_02_001: GAAP is a framework, not one rulebook — the Standards are the specific rules inside it. Check: framework or rule?
c12_acc_cbse_02_002: Goodwill exists once super-normal profits do — admission merely triggers the valuation. Check: earned or just priced?
c11_acc_cbse_02_002: The entity concept applies to sole proprietors too — household rent from business cash is Drawings. Check: business or personal?
c12_acc_cbse_02_003: Average only maintainable profit — strip one-offs, remuneration and abnormal items first. Check: raw or cleaned?
c11_acc_cbse_02_003: Purchased goodwill is recorded because a transaction proves it — internal brand value has none. Check: verifiable money evidence?
c12_acc_cbse_02_004: Capital employed excludes investments and fictitious assets — and profits get adjusted first. Check: really business capital?
c11_acc_cbse_02_004: Going concern means foreseeable future, not forever — even a loss-maker qualifies with funding. Check: intent, not age.
c12_acc_cbse_02_005: Revaluation raises then writes off goodwill; adjustment never touches the account. Check: which method is asked?
c11_acc_cbse_02_005: The period concept creates the need to allocate; accrual is the method that fulfils it. Check: need or method?
c12_acc_cbse_02_006: Unrecorded asset: Dr asset, Cr Revaluation — a gain. Unrecorded liability: reverse it. Check: gain or loss?
c11_acc_cbse_02_006: Cost fixes initial value but depreciation adjusts later; one transaction can touch three accounts. Check: two or more?
c12_acc_cbse_02_007: Reserves belong to old partners in the old ratio — past effort built them. Check: whose work made them?
c11_acc_cbse_02_007: Matching pairs period costs to the period using them; accrual tracks earning, not cash. Check: cash or event?
c12_acc_cbse_02_008: Capital adjustment can mean all partners' capitals, not just the newcomer's. Check: whose capital is aligned?
c11_acc_cbse_02_009: Consistency allows change with disclosure — and contingent items live in notes, not the Balance Sheet. Check: where disclosed?
c12_acc_cbse_02_010: Past items take the old ratio; goodwill premium the sacrificing; capital alignment the new. Check: which era?
c11_acc_cbse_02_010: Accrual follows the economic event, not the invoice — revenue counts on delivery. Check: billed or earned?
c12_acc_cbse_02_011: Hidden goodwill counts the new partner's capital inside total net assets — their money joins the firm. Check: whose money's in?
c11_acc_cbse_02_011: Standards are mandatory for companies — Sections 129/133 say so; disclosure covers alternatives. Check: optional or required?
c12_acc_cbse_03_001: Gaining ratio is new minus old share — not the new ratio itself. Check: gain per partner?
c11_acc_cbse_03_001: A business transaction needs value exchanged with an outside party — the family dinner doesn't count. Check: external or personal?
c12_acc_cbse_03_002: Retirement goodwill adjusts in the gaining ratio — new minus old, not the new ratio. Check: who gained how much?
c11_acc_cbse_03_002: The invoice is external evidence; the voucher is your internal authorisation. Check: which document proves it?
c12_acc_cbse_03_003: Revaluation adjusts book values while continuing; Realisation records actual sales on closing. Check: continuing or dissolving?
c11_acc_cbse_03_003: Rent paid is an expense, not a liability payoff — only outstanding rent is a liability. Check: owed or paid?
c12_acc_cbse_03_004: Reserves still split in the old ratio on retirement — the retiree earned past accumulations. Check: which ratio?
c11_acc_cbse_03_004: Debit isn't just 'increase' — a liability decrease is a debit. Check: which account class is moving?
c12_acc_cbse_03_005: The retiring due adds goodwill, revaluation and reserves to capital — the unpaid balance becomes a loan. Check: what's included?
c11_acc_cbse_03_005: Both take debits, but expenses shrink capital while assets are owned resources. Check: used up or held?
c12_acc_cbse_03_006: Mid-year profit is unknown — debit P&L Suspense for the deceased's estimated share. Check: known or estimated?
c11_acc_cbse_03_006: Bank is a Personal account — it's a separate legal entity; Drawings is Personal too. Check: real or personal?
c12_acc_cbse_03_007: Only the surrender value was booked — the excess claim is profit shared in the ratio. Check: what was recorded?
c11_acc_cbse_03_007: In the manual journal the credit goes on the next line, indented with 'To'. Check: is yours indented?
c12_acc_cbse_03_008: Use capital after all retirement adjustments — and subtract the retiree's paid-off capital first. Check: which balances?
c11_acc_cbse_03_008: In a compound entry, total debits must equal total credits — not each pair. Check the sums, not pairwise matches.
c12_acc_cbse_03_009: JLP proceeds aren't all the deceased's — it depends on how the policy was kept. Check: surrender or sum assured?
c11_acc_cbse_03_009: The ledger accumulates, not copies — five sales to Mohan become five debits in one account. Check: running balance?
c12_acc_cbse_03_010: Goodwill adjusts in the gaining ratio — new share minus old — not the new ratio. Check: who gained?
c11_acc_cbse_03_010: In Particulars, name the other account — the ledger already knows its own title. Check: source or itself?
c12_acc_cbse_04_001: Admission, retirement or death reconstitutes — it doesn't dissolve; prepare Revaluation, not Realisation. Check: firm continuing?
c11_acc_cbse_03_011: Balance c/d goes on the shorter side — debit side for liabilities and capital. Check: which side is smaller?
c12_acc_cbse_04_002: No written deed is needed — partnership can arise by conduct under Section 5. Check: conduct or paperwork?
c11_acc_cbse_04_001: The cash book still needs narration, and L.F. holds the ledger page — cash only, never credit sales. Check: cash or credit?
c12_acc_cbse_04_003: Realisation tracks asset sales and liability payments — settlement runs through Capital and Bank. Check: which account settles?
c11_acc_cbse_04_002: Discount columns are nominal — total and post them; there's no balance c/d. Check: balanced or totalled?
c12_acc_cbse_04_004: Who pays isn't who bears — the agreement decides bearing; the payer decides the credit. Check: whose burden?
c11_acc_cbse_04_003: The reimbursement restores the float in the main cash book — don't re-enter it as a petty receipt. Check: double-counted?
c12_acc_cbse_04_005: At dissolution the books close — Realisation captures the gain or loss directly, no ledger entries first. Check: closed or open?
c11_acc_cbse_04_004: Purchases Book is credit purchases of resale goods only — cash buys go to Cash Book. Check: both qualifiers met?
c12_acc_cbse_04_006: A partner's loan is a liability — settled before capital, and its interest is a charge. Check: creditor or owner?
c11_acc_cbse_04_005: On purchase return, Dr Supplier and Cr Purchases Return — think from your firm's books. Check: whose books?
c12_acc_cbse_04_007: A partner's loan ranks above partner capital under Section 48 — pay the creditor hat first. Check: which hat?
c11_acc_cbse_04_006: Journal Proper isn't rare — opening, closing and transfer entries land there yearly. Check: recurring or rare?
c12_acc_cbse_04_008: Insolvency deficiency is borne in the profit-sharing ratio here — Garner v Murray is the English rule. Check: which rule applies?
c11_acc_cbse_04_007: Day books hold nominal items — total and transfer to Trading/P&L; they aren't balanced. Check: balanced or totalled?
c12_acc_cbse_04_009: Realisation uses book values — the gap to realised value is the profit or loss. Check: book or sale value?
c11_acc_cbse_04_008: Contra entries are complete inside the cash book — posting again doubles the effect. Check: posted twice?
c12_acc_cbse_04_010: A partner taking an asset: Dr their Capital, Cr Realisation — track the claim, not the asset. Check: whose claim shrank?
c11_acc_cbse_04_009: Supplier and customer accounts post daily — only totals reach Purchases, Sales and GST. Check: items or totals?
c12_acc_cbse_05_001: Preference dividend is an appropriation — holders are owners, so skipping it isn't default. Check: creditor or owner?
c11_acc_cbse_05_001: The add/deduct direction depends on your starting balance — don't memorise signs. Check: which side did you start from?
c12_acc_cbse_05_002: Public, private or rights issue — the Application-Allotment-Calls mechanics are identical. Check: what differs?
c11_acc_cbse_05_002: The bank debits your account when the cheque is presented and paid — not when you issued it. Check presentation dates when reconciling.
c12_acc_cbse_05_003: Share Capital is credited at face value — discount goes to its own account, premium to Securities Premium. Check: face or issue price?
c11_acc_cbse_05_003: 'Deposited but not collected = deduct' only works from the cash book — other starts flip it. Check: where did you begin?
c12_acc_cbse_05_004: Excess application money funds allotment and calls first — only the leftover refunds. Check: refunded first?
c11_acc_cbse_05_004: Bank charges and bank interest appear in the passbook first — your cash book lags. Check: which book knows?
c12_acc_cbse_05_005: Calls in Arrears is deducted in the Notes under Share Capital — not just netted on the face. Check: where shown?
c11_acc_cbse_05_005: Money reaching the bank doesn't update your cash book — a direct deposit raises the passbook first. Check: which book moved?
c12_acc_cbse_05_006: Debit the asset at the agreed consideration, not face value — the difference adjusts Premium. Check: which value?
c11_acc_cbse_05_006: A dishonoured cheque means the bank reversed the credit — subtract it to reach the passbook. Check: which way?
c12_acc_cbse_05_007: On forfeiture, debit Securities Premium only if never received; credit Forfeited with what was paid. Check: premium received?
c11_acc_cbse_05_007: An unrectified error adjusts inside the BRS — no journal needed; bank errors never get one. Check: whose error?
c12_acc_cbse_05_008: Re-issue discount is capped at the forfeited amount and gains go to Capital Reserve. Check: which reserve?
c11_acc_cbse_05_008: 'Unpresented = add' flips under overdraft — your cash book shows more overdraft than the bank. Check: which is ahead?
c12_acc_cbse_05_009: Buyback premium is a return of capital — debit Securities Premium then free reserves, never P&L. Check: loss or capital?
c11_acc_cbse_05_009: Adjustment signs flip with the starting point and overdrafts — ask what the item does to your start. Check: higher or lower?
c12_acc_cbse_05_010: Paid-up isn't just issued minus arrears — count called-up, forfeited paid parts, calls in advance. Check: all pieces in?
c11_acc_cbse_05_010: Overdraft reconciliation flips every sign — unpresented cheques mean the bank shows less overdraft. Check: which book is ahead?
c12_acc_cbse_06_001: Secured/unsecured asks if a charge exists; first/second asks its ranking — second can still be secured. Check: which question?
c11_acc_cbse_06_001: A tallied Trial Balance isn't proof — principle, omission and compensating errors hide inside. Check: equal or right?
c12_acc_cbse_06_002: Debentures credit at face value even at discount — debit the discount separately as a capital loss. Check: face or issue?
c11_acc_cbse_06_002: A zero-balance account still goes in the Trial Balance — show it with zero. Check: is it listed?
c12_acc_cbse_06_003: Divide consideration by issue price, not face value — a 10% discount means more debentures. Check: which divisor?
c11_acc_cbse_06_003: An error breaks the TB only if one-sided — wrong account with right amounts still tallies. Check: one or two sides?
c12_acc_cbse_06_004: Collateral debentures record at full face value issued — the margin is the lender's cushion. Check: loan or face?
c11_acc_cbse_06_004: Machinery in the Purchases Book breaks capital-vs-revenue — that's a principle error. Check: commission or principle?
c12_acc_cbse_06_005: Debenture interest is always on face value, not issue price — a 9% debenture pays 9% of ₹100 even if issued at ₹95. Check the nominal value.
c11_acc_cbse_06_005: Complete omission keeps the TB tallied — only partial omission breaks it. Check: one side posted?
c12_acc_cbse_06_006: Loss on issue adds the redemption premium too — look at cash out at maturity, not just issue. Check: both ends?
c11_acc_cbse_06_006: A wrong amount in the original book hits both sides equally — the TB still tallies. Check: one or two-sided?
c12_acc_cbse_06_007: Draw of lots redeems only the drawn debentures — the rest stay live liabilities. Check: all or drawn?
c11_acc_cbse_06_007: Compensating errors sit in different accounts — same-account offsets are just two errors. Check: where do they sit?
c12_acc_cbse_06_008: Own debentures get cancelled immediately — and the profit on cancellation is capital, not interest. Check: held or cancelled?
c11_acc_cbse_06_008: Suspense is for one-sided errors only — two-sided ones get a direct correcting entry. Check: did the TB break?
c12_acc_cbse_06_009: DRR is appropriated profit, no asset; a sinking fund holds real investments. Check: entry or assets?
c11_acc_cbse_06_009: Suspense only absorbs one-sided net differences — two-sided errors get normal entries. Check: which kind?
c12_acc_cbse_06_010: Redemption premium is a liability owed at maturity — credit at issue, debit at redemption. Check: profit or liability?
c11_acc_cbse_06_010: P&L Adjustment is for nominal errors only — machinery still gets Dr Machinery, Cr Creditor. Check: which account class?
c12_acc_cbse_07_001: Schedule III mandates more than two statements — cash flow, equity changes, notes. Check: what's required?
c11_acc_cbse_07_001: Depreciation allocates cost over useful periods — it isn't a market-value fix. Check: cost or price?
c12_acc_cbse_07_002: Schedule III order is law — wrong classification breaks comparability and invites penalty. Check: the prescribed heads.
c11_acc_cbse_07_002: Depreciation covers obsolescence and expired rights too — a working computer still depreciates. Check: worn or obsolete?
c12_acc_cbse_07_003: The P&L isn't the old T-format — Schedule III prescribes sub-heads and splits exceptional items. Check: which format?
c11_acc_cbse_07_003: Cost includes freight, installation, trial runs — and residual is net of disposal. Check: both ends counted?
c12_acc_cbse_07_004: Calls in Arrears reduces subscribed capital — it never nets against Calls in Advance. Check: which head?
c11_acc_cbse_07_004: Under SLM the rate applies to cost minus scrap — derive it from the depreciable amount. Check: which base?
c12_acc_cbse_07_005: Unclaimed dividend is a certain liability — Other Current Liabilities, not a provision. Check: certain or estimated?
c11_acc_cbse_07_005: Under WDV apply the rate to the written-down value — each year's charge shrinks. Check: which base?
c12_acc_cbse_07_006: Share capital shows nominal value — issue discount goes to Other Non-Current Assets or is written off. Check: netted or separate?
c11_acc_cbse_07_006: WDV isn't automatically better — tax law isn't your books, and WDV never hits zero. Check: which factors weigh?
c12_acc_cbse_07_007: Classify by purpose — breeding livestock is PPE; loose tools are consumables, not fixed assets. Check: purpose or looks?
c11_acc_cbse_07_007: Crediting depreciation isn't money in — it allocates past cost; the credit goes to Depreciation. Check: income or allocation?
c12_acc_cbse_07_008: Managerial pay sits inside Employee Benefits — the break-up goes to Notes; 5% vs 11% differ. Check: which limit?
c11_acc_cbse_07_008: Under the provision method the asset stays at cost — credit the Provision account. Check: asset or provision?
c12_acc_cbse_07_009: Accumulated depreciation is a contra-asset, not a liability — a provision is a charge, a reserve an appropriation. Check: which side?
c11_acc_cbse_07_009: A provision is charged even in loss years; a reserve is an appropriation of profit. Check: charge or appropriation?
c12_acc_cbse_07_010: Every adjustment hits twice — expense up in P&L, liability up on the Balance Sheet. Check: both effects?
c11_acc_cbse_07_010: A reserve fund is just an entry — no cash moves until the firm invests it. Check: did money move?
c12_acc_cbse_07_011: Schedule III keeps the face condensed — outstanding and prepaid sit inside main heads. Check: face or notes?
c11_acc_cbse_07_011: Provision for depreciation spreads cost — it isn't profit kept aside for replacement. Check: matching or retaining?
c12_acc_cbse_08_001: A ratio is a whistle-blower, not the answer — compare to industry and past years first. Check: compared to what?
c11_acc_cbse_07_012: A secret reserve needs deliberate under-statement — land appreciating is just an unrealised gain. Check: created or observed?
c12_acc_cbse_08_002: Data limits hit all analysis; ratio limits are specific to ratios — keep the two lists separate. Check: which limit?
c11_acc_cbse_08_001: Ask whether the spend brings future benefit — a life-extending overhaul is capital; big rent isn't. Check: benefit ahead?
c12_acc_cbse_08_003: Comparative statements are the tool; horizontal analysis is the act — compute absolute and % change. Check: stated or analysed?
c11_acc_cbse_08_002: Factory location doesn't make a cost direct — supervisor salary and insurance are indirect. Check: for the specific product?
c12_acc_cbse_08_004: % change uses last year as base — decreases need brackets; a zero base means 'not comparable'. Check: which base?
c11_acc_cbse_08_003: Production wages go to Trading, office salaries to P&L — combined figures without factory detail sit in P&L. Check: which split?
c12_acc_cbse_08_005: Percentages mislead alone — a small % on a big base can outweigh a big % on revenue. Check: the absolute change.
c11_acc_cbse_08_004: Factory rent and carriage inwards are direct — they go to Trading, not P&L. Check: which account?
c12_acc_cbse_08_006: Common-size Balance Sheet uses the grand total as base for both sides — with % signs. Check: which base?
c11_acc_cbse_08_005: Direct expenses already in Trading mustn't re-enter P&L — that's double-counting. Check: counted twice?
c12_acc_cbse_08_007: Common-size P&L divides everything by Revenue from Operations — not total expenses. Check: which denominator?
c11_acc_cbse_08_006: Closing stock isn't in the Trial Balance — it enters via the adjustment entry. Check: opening or closing?
c12_acc_cbse_08_008: Pick a normal base year — no strikes or one-offs; trend % is current ÷ base × 100. Check: is the base normal?
c11_acc_cbse_08_007: Fixed vs current isn't physical — goodwill is non-current, prepaids can be current. Check: the operating cycle.
c12_acc_cbse_08_009: Internal uses transaction detail to fix operations; external uses aggregates to judge. Check: which question, which data?
c11_acc_cbse_08_008: Not every bank loan is non-current — the portion due within 12 months is current. Check: the repayment schedule.
c12_acc_cbse_09_001: The cash flow statement isn't the cash book — for non-financial firms, interest paid is financing. Check: firm's type?
c11_acc_cbse_02_008: Consistency allows a disclosed change — disclosure lives in notes, not the Balance Sheet. Check: where does it sit?
c11_acc_cbse_08_009: Closing stock cuts cost of goods sold — it credits Trading, it isn't income. Check: which account credited?
c11_acc_cbse_08_010: Easy to flip these — outstanding gets added to the expense (liability), prepaid gets deducted (asset). Check which way you adjusted.
c11_acc_cbse_08_011: Watch the wording: income earned but not received is your right to collect — an asset, not a liability. Check: receivable or payable?
c11_acc_cbse_08_012: No cash moves for depreciation or bad debts — they adjust values, not the bank column. Check whether Bank should really be credited.
c11_acc_cbse_09_001: Adjustments aren't error-fixes — they split each amount into this period's share and the next's, for incomes too. Check both sides.
c11_acc_cbse_09_002: Closing stock credits Trading to cut COGS — it isn't revenue; in the TB it's already adjusted. Check: revenue or reduction?
c11_acc_cbse_09_003: The expense account holds only the paid part — debit it for the unpaid bit, credit a liability. Check: paid or owed?
c11_acc_cbse_09_004: It's easy to reverse these — ask: do you have a right to receive (asset) or an obligation to give (liability)? Check which side you debited.
c11_acc_cbse_09_005: Depreciation isn't cash saved for a new asset — it spreads the old one's cost. Check: fund or allocation?
c11_acc_cbse_09_006: 'Provision' sounds like money set aside, but it's a valuation cut — deduct it from Debtors on the assets side. Check where you showed it.
c11_acc_cbse_09_007: Discount on debtors uses 'good debtors' — deduct further bad debts AND the new doubtful-debts provision first. Check your base figure.
c11_acc_cbse_09_008: Don't net these — interest on capital cuts profit, interest on drawings raises it. Check: which way does each go?
c11_acc_cbse_09_009: On approval there's no sale yet — reverse it and return goods to stock at cost. Check: sale or approval?
c11_acc_cbse_09_010: 'After charging commission' means base = profit minus the commission — use rate/(100+rate). Check: which base?
c11_acc_cbse_09_011: Every adjustment lands twice — e.g., depreciation cuts profit AND the asset's book value. Check the second effect made the Balance Sheet.
c11_bio_cbse_01_001: Fire 'grows' and 'breathes', but without cells, enzymes or inheritance it isn't alive. Check the mechanism, not the surface similarity.
c11_bio_cbse_01_002: A crystal adds material outside; living growth builds new cells inside via metabolism and division. Check where the growth comes from.
c11_bio_cbse_01_003: Cellular organisation means hierarchy — cell to tissue to organ — not just 'made of cells'. And plants do respond. Check the definition.
c11_bio_cbse_01_004: Whales swim like fish but classify with mammals — classification tracks shared ancestry, not looks. Check the evolutionary link first.
c11_bio_cbse_01_005: Species isn't just 'looks alike' — it's interbreeding populations, and even that fails for asexual life. Check which criterion applies.
c11_bio_cbse_01_006: A botanical garden isn't a park — its plants are documented wild-origin accessions in taxonomic order. Check for provenance records.
c11_bio_cbse_01_007: It's tempting to capitalise 'indica' like a proper noun — but the epithet is always lowercase; only the genus gets a capital. Check it.
c11_bio_cbse_01_008: A key isn't picture-matching — you answer paired contrasting traits step by step. Check each couplet, not the overall look.
c11_bio_cbse_02_001: Five kingdoms isn't the final word — Protista's edges are 'not well defined' and the three-domain system came later. Check the caveat.
c11_bio_cbse_02_002: 'Blue-green algae' aren't algae — no nucleus, 70S ribosomes and a peptidoglycan wall put them in Monera. Check the cell type, not colour.
c11_bio_cbse_02_003: An endospore isn't offspring — one cell, one spore, one cell again. Check: did the count increase?
c11_bio_cbse_02_004: Euglena photosynthesises but isn't a plant — protists are defined by eukaryotic cell features, not one trait. Check cell structure first.
c11_bio_cbse_02_005: Dikaryotic isn't diploid — two haploid nuclei share one cytoplasm without fusing. Check whether karyogamy has happened.
c11_bio_cbse_02_006: A lichen's hyphae wrap each algal cell — and it has no roots, absorbing over its whole surface. Check: roots or surface?
c11_bio_cbse_02_007: A fern doesn't morph like a caterpillar — sporophyte and gametophyte are separate plants alternating. Check which generation you're seeing.
c11_bio_cbse_02_008: 'Eats other organisms' doesn't make an animal — Cuscuta is a parasitic plant, fungi absorb food. Check the nutrition mechanism.
c11_bio_cbse_02_009: Viruses copy themselves only inside a host and have no metabolism — no ATP, no ribosomes. Viroids even lack a capsid. Check the machinery.
c11_bio_cbse_02_010: Prions spread disease but they're proteins, not cells — and lichen is mutualism, not a moss. Check what it's made of.
c11_bio_cbse_03_001: Cryptogams aren't all non-vascular — ferns have xylem and phloem. Seeds evolved before flowers. Check the trait order, not 'lower/higher'.
c11_bio_cbse_03_002: Not all algae have flagella — red algae have none at any stage, and brown algal spores bear two unequal lateral ones. Check the class.
c11_bio_cbse_03_003: Brown and red algae do have chlorophyll a — fucoxanthin and phycoerythrin just mask the green. Check for accessory pigments.
c11_bio_cbse_03_004: In mosses the leafy plant is the gametophyte — the sporophyte is just the stalked capsule on top. Check which generation the 'plant' is.
c11_bio_cbse_03_005: A fern's prothallus isn't a dependent blob — it's a free-living, photosynthetic gametophyte the sporophyte grows from. Check the life cycle.
c11_bio_cbse_03_006: In pines, pollination and fertilisation sit about a year apart — the female gametophyte matures meanwhile. Check the timeline.
c11_bio_cbse_03_007: Two male gametes, two targets — one fuses with the egg (zygote), the other with polar nuclei (endosperm). Check the zygote is 2n.
c11_bio_cbse_03_008: The generations aren't twins — gametophyte rules mosses, sporophyte ferns; meiosis makes spores. Check: which dominates?
c11_bio_cbse_03_009: Algin and carrageen aren't stored food — they're cell-wall polysaccharides; laminarin is the storage carb. Check where it sits in the cell.
c11_bio_cbse_04_001: Radial doesn't mean diploblastic — starfish are triploblastic coelomates with secondary radial symmetry. Check germ layers, not shape.
c11_bio_cbse_04_002: Flatworms have organs, but not coordinated systems — organ-system level needs functional integration. Check if organs work as a unit.
c11_bio_cbse_04_003: Two cell layers aren't two germ layers — sponges skip gastrulation, so 'diploblastic' doesn't apply. Check embryonic origin, not layers.
c11_bio_cbse_04_004: A jellyfish 'nerve net' is diffuse with no brain — impulses spread, but there's no processing or decision. Check for centralisation.
c11_bio_cbse_04_005: Comb jellies aren't stinging jellyfish — they grip prey with colloblasts, not nematocysts. Check the cell type, not the gel body.
c11_bio_cbse_04_006: Acoelomate means no mesoderm-LINED cavity — flatworms still have solid mesoderm and are triploblastic. Check the germ layer count.
c11_bio_cbse_04_007: 'Pseudo' doesn't mean useless — the pseudocoelom is a working hydrostatic skeleton with a full gut. Check its function, not its name.
c11_bio_cbse_04_008: True segmentation repeats organs inside — nephridia, vessels, nerves — not just outer rings. Check what's repeated internally.
c11_bio_cbse_04_009: Open circulation doesn't mean blood carries oxygen — insects deliver O2 by tracheal tubes; haemolymph lacks haemoglobin. Check the carrier.
c11_bio_cbse_04_010: Not every mollusc is snail-shaped — bivalves have no radula and octopus has no outer shell. Check the class before assuming the plan.
c11_bio_cbse_04_011: Starfish radial symmetry is secondary — their larvae are bilateral, and they're triploblastic coelomates unlike cnidarians. Check the larva.
c11_bio_cbse_04_012: The 'half chordate' stomochord is just a gut out-pouching, not a notochord — and the main nerve cord is ventral and solid. Check its origin.
c11_bio_cbse_04_013: Protochordates aren't vertebrates-in-waiting — and it's the notochord that defines chordates. Check: which structure?
c11_bio_cbse_04_014: Sharks have no operculum — separate gill slits and placoid scales. And crocodiles have four-chambered hearts. Check the exceptions.
c11_bio_cbse_05_001: Underground doesn't mean root — potato 'eyes' are nodes with buds, which roots never have. Check for nodes before naming it.
c11_bio_cbse_05_002: A potato is a stem tuber — it has nodes ('eyes'), scale leaves and grows from a stolon tip, not a radicle. Check the buds.
c11_bio_cbse_05_003: Phyllotaxy is leaves on the stem; venation is veins inside a leaf — mango is alternate AND reticulate. Check which level you mean.
c11_bio_cbse_05_004: 'Determinate' doesn't mean the plant stops — only the main axis ends in a flower while side branches keep growing. Check the laterals.
c11_bio_cbse_05_005: Aestivation is petals in bud; placentation is ovules in the ovary — pea is vexillary AND marginal. Check which structure you mean.
c11_bio_cbse_05_006: Syncarpous means fused carpels, not one — and epipetalous (stamen on petal) isn't epiphyllous (on perianth). Check the attachment.
c11_bio_cbse_05_007: Sweet and edible isn't a fruit — ask the tissue: strawberry's fruits are the achenes. Check: which tissue grew it?
c11_bio_cbse_05_008: A maize 'seed' is really a fruit — the pericarp fuses to the seed coat, so the outer layer is fruit wall, not testa. Check the label.
c11_bio_cbse_05_009: A floral formula isn't just counts — brackets show fusion, a line shows adhesion, and the ovary line marks superior/inferior. Check symbols.
c11_bio_cbse_05_010: Brackets fuse parts within a whorl; a line above joins different whorls — epipetalous stamens get a line, not brackets. Check which fusion.
c11_bio_cbse_06_001: Meristems aren't only at tips — cambium thickens trunks and intercalary meristems regrow grass after mowing. Check all three locations.
c11_bio_cbse_06_002: Both give support, but collenchyma stays living and stretchy in growing parts while sclerenchyma is dead and rigid. Check where it's found.
c11_bio_cbse_06_003: Phloem moves food, not water — xylem does that passively. Girdling kills because roots starve, not because water stops. Check the cargo.
c11_bio_cbse_06_004: Monocot root 'polyarch' means many alternating xylem-phloem arms in a ring — not the scattered bundles of the stem. Check the arrangement.
c11_bio_cbse_06_005: 'Closed' means no cambium sits between xylem and phloem — not that they don't touch. Check for cambium, not contact.
c11_bio_cbse_06_006: Dorsiventral vs isobilateral is about mesophyll — palisade+spongy vs uniform — not the two epidermises. Check the mesophyll first.
c11_bio_cbse_06_007: One ring isn't one division — each cambial initial divides many times a season, and the ring is the year's cumulative wood. Check the zone.
c11_bio_cbse_06_008: In roots, cambium arises from conjunctive tissue AND pericycle — and cork cambium also comes from pericycle, not cortex. Check the origin.
c11_bio_cbse_06_009: 'Anomalous' growth isn't disease — it's a normal variant, and the mechanism differs per plant. Check which cambium pattern it is.
c11_bio_cbse_06_010: Bamboo has no vascular cambium, so no true wood or rings — and cork cambium is living. Check: can it ring?
c11_bio_cbse_07_001: In stratified epithelium only the basal cells divide and touch the basement membrane — surface cells just shed. Check where mitosis happens.
c11_bio_cbse_07_002: 'Connective' isn't about glue — blood, bone and fat all qualify by mesodermal origin and a cells-in-matrix plan. Check the criteria.
c11_bio_cbse_07_003: Filaments don't shrink — actin and myosin keep their length and slide to overlap. Check: filament length in the diagram?
c11_bio_cbse_07_004: You might picture the impulse as electrons flowing down a wire — really each patch of membrane fires fresh. Check: does Na+ enter locally?
c11_bio_cbse_07_005: Frogs never sip water — you absorb it through the belly skin, and the tongue is only for catching prey. Check: which surface takes in water?
c11_bio_cbse_07_006: The cloaca isn't just an anus — it's a chambered outlet handling faeces, urine and gametes separately. Check: can you name its regions?
c11_bio_cbse_07_007: Skin breathing alone can't fuel a jump — it's slow, needs moist skin, and lungs kick in when demand rises. Check: when must lungs take over?
c11_bio_cbse_07_008: One ventricle doesn't mean half-mixed blood — the spiral valve streams oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor apart. Check: which arch gets which?
c11_bio_cbse_07_009: A frog brain isn't a mini human brain — olfactory and optic lobes dominate and the cerebellum stays tiny. Check: which lobe is biggest?
c11_bio_cbse_08_001: Viruses aren't 'non-living' just for lacking cells — they can't run metabolism or reproduce alone. Check: can it live outside a host?
c11_bio_cbse_08_002: Prokaryotes aren't primitive — they respire, fix nitrogen and photosynthesise without any organelles. Check: name one complex job they do.
c11_bio_cbse_08_003: The membrane isn't a free-drifting liquid — rafts, cytoskeleton fences and junctions corral proteins. Check: what limits the drifting?
c11_bio_cbse_08_004: The wall isn't a static brick shell — it grows actively in layers, and plasmodesmata are gated. Check: why is a root-tip wall thin?
c11_bio_cbse_08_005: Lysosomes bud from the Golgi, not the ER — and they recycle your own cell parts, not just waste. Check: which organelle ships them?
c11_bio_cbse_08_006: Plants need mitochondria too — chloroplasts fix carbon; mitochondria burn sugar day and night. Check: what powers a dark seed?
c11_bio_cbse_08_007: S isn't size, and 50S+30S isn't 80S — sedimentation depends on shape as well as mass. Check: why don't subunits add up?
c11_bio_cbse_08_008: Chromatin and chromosomes are the same DNA-histone mix, just condensed or relaxed. Check: same molecule or two different ones?
c11_bio_cbse_08_009: A vacuole isn't a passive water bag — its membrane pumps solutes in to build turgor. Check: does a plant cell even have centrioles?
c11_bio_cbse_08_010: Peroxisomes aren't mini-lysosomes — they run oxidative reactions and bud from the ER, not the Golgi. Check: do they carry acid hydrolases?
c11_bio_cbse_09_001: Polymers still keep one free anomeric end, so starch gives a faint Benedict's result. Check: where is the reducing end?
c11_bio_cbse_09_002: The peptide bond can't rotate freely — resonance gives it partial double-bond character, flat and rigid. Check: which angles twist?
c11_bio_cbse_09_003: Not every lipid is a fat — membranes are built from phospholipids, and cholesterol and waxes count too. Check: which lipid makes membranes?
c11_bio_cbse_09_004: Base pairing isn't arbitrary — H-bond donors and acceptors must match, and strands run 5' to 3'. Check: did you label the ends?
c11_bio_cbse_09_005: Enzymes leave each reaction unchanged — one can process thousands of substrates a second. Check: is the enzyme in the products?
c11_bio_cbse_09_006: Cold only pauses an enzyme — it wakes on rewarming, unlike heat which denatures for good. Check: can chilling be undone?
c11_bio_cbse_09_007: Cytosolic NADH can't cross into mitochondria directly — shuttles hand it in at different ATP rates. Check: which shuttle does muscle use?
c11_bio_cbse_09_008: Metabolism is building and breaking together, and steady state isn't equilibrium — flux keeps running. Check: is anything still flowing?
c11_bio_cbse_09_009: Macro vs micro is set by acid solubility, not polymer status — lipids land in the macro fraction. Check: was it precipitated by TCA?
c11_bio_cbse_10_001: Interphase only looks quiet — the cell is growing, copying its DNA and prepping checkpoints throughout. Check: when is DNA replicated?
c11_bio_cbse_10_002: After S phase the DNA doubles but chromosome count doesn't — count centromeres, not chromatids. Check: how many centromeres?
c11_bio_cbse_10_003: Prophase only reveals already-copied chromosomes — replication happened back in S phase. Check: when did the DNA actually double?
c11_bio_cbse_10_004: In anaphase the centromere leads and the arms trail behind — not the other way round. Check: which end points at the pole?
c11_bio_cbse_10_005: Most of your cells never divide again — neurons rest in G0, and only plant meristems keep going. Check: does heart muscle grow by mitosis?
c11_bio_cbse_10_006: Crossing over happens back in pachytene — chiasmata just mark where it already occurred. Check: alignment stage or recombination stage?
c11_bio_cbse_10_007: Meiosis II doesn't halve chromosomes again — n stays n; only the DNA content drops. Check: centromere count after meiosis II?
c11_bio_cbse_10_008: Crossing over swaps between non-sister chromatids of homologues, not identical sisters. Check: whose arms are exchanging?
c11_bio_cbse_11_001: Accessory pigments harvest about a third of the light and guard against damage. Check: which colours do they catch?
c11_bio_cbse_11_002: Lumen protons also come from splitting water, not just pumping — and the lumen turns acidic. Check: which side sits near pH 5?
c11_bio_cbse_11_003: Protons reach the lumen from water splitting and pumping while the stroma loses them to NADP+. Check: where does pH drop to ~5?
c11_bio_cbse_11_004: The cycle doesn't spit out glucose each turn — five of six G3P rebuild RuBP. Check: how many turns per net glucose?
c11_bio_cbse_11_005: C4 plants still run the Calvin cycle — it's tucked into bundle sheath cells behind a CO2 pump. Check: where does RuBisCO act?
c11_bio_cbse_11_006: Photorespiration isn't photosynthesis in reverse — it burns glycolate across three organelles and costs ATP. Check: is glucose oxidised?
c11_bio_cbse_11_007: More of a factor isn't always better — light saturates and can even inhibit. Check: which factor is the real bottleneck now?
c11_bio_cbse_11_008: Light doesn't pour into glucose — it changes hands via ATP, NADPH and a proton gradient. Check: which currency pays?
c11_bio_cbse_12_001: Roots breathe straight from soil air, not oxygen shipped down the phloem — and stems use lenticels. Check: where does root O2 come from?
c11_bio_cbse_12_002: Your two glycolysis NADH don't automatically make 6 ATP — shuttles can drop them to 2 each. Check: which shuttle is assumed?
c11_bio_cbse_12_003: Fermentation doesn't make NAD+ — it recycles it so glycolysis can keep running. Check: what stops without it?
c11_bio_cbse_12_004: Pyruvate oxidation happens inside the mitochondria, not the cytoplasm — and it releases your first CO2. Check: where does acetyl-CoA form?
c11_bio_cbse_12_005: The CO2 released this turn isn't the acetyl-CoA that just entered — those carbons leave a turn later. Check: whose carbons exit?
c11_bio_cbse_12_006: 38 ATP is a textbook ceiling, not a promise — shuttles, proton leaks and diversions shave it down. Check: which shuttle is assumed?
c11_bio_cbse_12_007: 38 ATP assumes the malate-aspartate shuttle and no diversions — real cells usually net ~30-32. Check: what does muscle get?
c11_bio_cbse_12_008: Amphibolic doesn't mean the cycle runs backwards — intermediates are siphoned off at branch points. Check: does Krebs ever reverse?
c11_bio_cbse_13_001: A swollen seed isn't growing yet — that's just water uptake; growth needs irreversible metabolism. Check: can the change be undone?
c11_bio_cbse_13_002: The root tip's phases are places, not ages — a cell's stage depends on its distance from the apex. Check: where is the cell sitting?
c11_bio_cbse_13_003: Auxin never enters the lateral bud — it suppresses it indirectly through nutrients and stem signals. Check: does bud-applied auxin inhibit?
c11_bio_cbse_13_004: GA and cytokinin aren't a team everywhere — one stretches stems, the other frees buds. Check: which delays leaf yellowing?
c11_bio_cbse_13_005: Ethylene isn't only a ripener and ABA isn't only an abscission signal — context decides the job. Check: what is ABA's main role?
c11_bio_cbse_13_006: Plants measure the night, not the day — one red flash in darkness can cancel flowering. Check: long-night or short-day?
c11_bio_cbse_13_007: Cold only makes the plant able to flower — it still needs the right photoperiod after. Check: what does vernalisation buy?
c11_bio_cbse_13_008: A dormant seed isn't dead — it breathes slowly and keeps sensing light and temperature. Check: does it still respire?
c11_bio_cbse_14_001: No gas swaps in the bronchi — their walls are too thick; exchange starts at respiratory bronchioles. Check: where do capillaries appear?
c11_bio_cbse_14_002: Normal breathing out is passive recoil — muscles only join in when you force it. Check: which muscles work at rest?
c11_bio_cbse_14_003: CO2's gradient is actually small — it crosses easily because it's far more soluble. Check: each gas's mmHg difference?
c11_bio_cbse_14_004: High CO2 unloads O2 in tissues, but in the lungs the shift reverses to load it. Check: which way does the curve shift where?
c11_bio_cbse_14_005: CO2 crosses the membrane itself — the chloride shift only swaps out the bicarbonate it became. Check: what leaves the RBC?
c11_bio_cbse_14_006: CO2, not O2, runs your everyday breathing — oxygen only takes charge below ~60 mmHg. Check: what do central receptors sense?
c11_bio_cbse_14_007: Asthma squeezes airways reversibly; emphysema destroys the exchange surface for good. Check: can the damage be reversed?
c11_bio_cbse_15_001: Not every white cell engulfs — B cells make antibodies while T cells coordinate or kill. Check: which cell makes antibodies?
c11_bio_cbse_15_002: An O parent still passes on the i allele — with an AB partner, a B child is possible. Check: which alleles combine?
c11_bio_cbse_15_003: Artery means away from the heart, not oxygen-rich — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood. Check: which way does it flow?
c11_bio_cbse_15_004: Lub-dub is valves snapping shut under pressure — not the heart muscle thumping. Check: which valve closes for S1?
c11_bio_cbse_15_005: The two circuits run in series — a failing left ventricle backs pressure into the lungs. Check: whose output feeds the right heart?
c11_bio_cbse_15_006: Both systems are always somewhat on — stress first lifts the vagal brake, then sympathetic rises. Check: what changes in the first second?
c11_bio_cbse_15_007: High pressure injures vessel walls, plaque stiffens them, pressure climbs — they feed each other. Check: which starts the cycle?
c11_bio_cbse_15_008: Lymph isn't blood minus red cells — it drains one way, pushed by muscle squeeze. Check: where do absorbed fats first go?
c11_bio_cbse_16_001: Most nephrons have short loops and never reach deep medulla — only juxtamedullary ones build the gradient. Check: which type concentrates?
c11_bio_cbse_16_002: Filtrate concentrates going down the loop but dilutes going up — don't draw a straight rise. Check: which limb loses salt?
c11_bio_cbse_16_003: Filtration fraction can shift — squeezing the efferent keeps GFR while plasma flow falls. Check: which arteriole constricted?
c11_bio_cbse_16_004: Water only follows salt where the wall allows it — the ascending limb stays watertight. Check: is ADH acting here?
c11_bio_cbse_16_005: Antidiuretic means less urine — ADH opens water channels while aldosterone works on sodium. Check: which hormone adds aquaporins?
c11_bio_cbse_16_006: Urine isn't fixed — volume, osmolarity and solutes all swing with your intake and hormones. Check: what does a salty meal change?
c11_bio_cbse_16_007: Dialysis only drifts small solutes out — it can't reabsorb, secrete or replace kidney hormones. Check: what's missing vs a nephron?
c11_bio_cbse_16_008: The liver dumps wastes into bile and out with faeces — the kidney handles urine. Check: which route does bilirubin take?
c11_bio_cbse_17_001: Cilia aren't tiny muscles — they beat with dynein sliding microtubules, not actin-myosin. Check: what's inside a 9+2 axoneme?
c11_bio_cbse_17_002: Striped doesn't mean voluntary — cardiac muscle is striated yet beats entirely on its own. Check: where does cardiac fit the table?
c11_bio_cbse_17_003: In a contraction nothing shrinks — actin and myosin keep their length and slide past each other. Check: which bands narrow?
c11_bio_cbse_17_004: Calcium doesn't bind actin — it binds troponin, which drags tropomyosin off the sites. Check: what does Ca2+ touch first?
c11_bio_cbse_17_005: The sternum is three fused parts, and only the first seven rib pairs attach straight to it. Check: where do ribs 11-12 go?
c11_bio_cbse_17_006: Hinge and pivot aren't separate classes — they're subtypes within synovial joints. Check: which class does the knee belong to?
c11_bio_cbse_17_007: Osteoporosis isn't just low calcium — bone is lost faster than rebuilt while blood Ca stays normal. Check: is serum calcium low?
c11_bio_cbse_18_001: A unipolar neuron's single branch still does a dendrite's job — carrying the signal toward the cell body. Check: which way does it conduct?
c11_bio_cbse_18_002: The impulse isn't a current sliding down the axon — each patch of membrane fires the next. Check: where does Na+ actually enter?
c11_bio_cbse_18_003: Nothing jumps the synaptic cleft electrically — a transmitter molecule floats across to the next cell. Check: what crosses the gap?
c11_bio_cbse_18_004: The cortex isn't everything — limbic structures run memory and emotion, the brainstem rhythm. Check: where does memory consolidate?
c11_bio_cbse_18_005: Your spinal cord ends near L1-L2 — lower nerves dangle as the cauda equina. Check: which segment does a T12 fracture hit?
c11_bio_cbse_18_006: You have 8 cervical nerves but only 7 cervical vertebrae — C1 exits above the atlas. Check: which nerve does a C5-C6 disc pinch?
c11_bio_cbse_18_007: A reflex starts in the cord but the brain still hears about it — and can dampen or boost it. Check: can you suppress a knee-jerk?
c11_bio_cbse_18_008: The cornea does most of the focusing — the lens fine-tunes by getting fatter, not by moving. Check: which supplies ~43D?
c11_bio_cbse_18_009: The cochlea maps pitch by place along the membrane — and loudness by how many fibres fire. Check: where do high notes peak?
c11_bio_cbse_19_001: ADH and oxytocin are made in the hypothalamus — the posterior pituitary only stores and releases them. Check: where are the cell bodies?
c11_bio_cbse_19_002: PTH, not calcitonin, runs your blood calcium — and it comes from the parathyroids, not the thyroid. Check: what raises blood Ca?
c11_bio_cbse_19_003: Glucagon can't pull glucose out of muscle — muscle lacks the enzyme to export it. Check: which tissue has glucose-6-phosphatase?
c11_bio_cbse_19_004: The adrenal halves take different orders — medulla fires on nerve signals, cortex waits on ACTH. Check: which rises first in fright?
c11_bio_cbse_19_005: LH doesn't make estrogen directly — it feeds theca androgens that granulosa cells aromatise. Check: which cells does FSH act on?
c11_bio_cbse_19_006: Glands aren't the only hormone sources — your heart, kidney and gut secrete them too. Check: which hormone does the kidney release?
c11_bio_cbse_19_007: Steroids aren't always slow — some act at membrane receptors in seconds, and peptides can tweak genes. Check: is it always via DNA?
c11_bio_cbse_19_008: A goitre means the gland was urged to grow — it can be hypo, hyper or even euthyroid. Check: what's driving the enlargement?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_001: Biotech isn't only gene editing — fermentation and classical microbial products count too. Check: is penicillin 'modern' biotech?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_002: Discoveries didn't march in order — DNA was found in 1869, but its structure only in 1953. Check: who discovered DNA itself?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_003: Traditional vs modern isn't about the year — it's whole-organism empiricism vs rational gene design. Check: is isolated DNA manipulated?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_004: The biotech colours mark the sector, not the method — red is health, green is agriculture. Check: which colour is industrial?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_005: Bt protein isn't a persistent pesticide — it's insect-specific and degrades in soil within days. Check: does it harm other insects?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_006: A recombinant vaccine delivers antigen, not a gene cure — Hep B vaccine is purified protein. Check: does any gene enter you?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_007: Industrial fermentation isn't all anaerobic — penicillin and citric acid need oxygen. Check: is the product growth-linked?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_008: Phytoremediation isn't just planting — metals must be harvested or locked, and only hyperaccumulators cope. Check: is yours one?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_009: Bioethics isn't a gut feeling or a safety certificate — it weighs principles like autonomy and justice. Check: which principle applies?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_010: The host's safety class isn't enough — rDNA work starts at BSL-2 and the insert sets the risk. Check: what gene did you clone?
c11_biotech_cbse_01_011: A GMO isn't automatically patentable in India — plants and animals are excluded; only microbes qualify. Check: what is being patented?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_001: 70S ribosomes don't prove 'prokaryote' — your own mitochondria and chloroplasts carry them. Check: which compartment holds them?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_002: Membrane proteins don't all drift freely — cytoskeleton fences and lipid rafts corral many. Check: why do receptors cluster?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_003: A cell wall isn't uniform brickwork — it remodels as the cell differentiates and defends. Check: what besides cellulose is in it?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_004: Ribosomes aren't glued to the rough ER — they dock only while making a secreted protein. Check: what decides where one sits?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_005: The Golgi doesn't make proteins or lipids — it modifies and ships what the ER built. Check: where was the protein synthesised?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_006: A burst lysosome won't digest the cell — its enzymes stall at neutral pH and the membrane resists them. Check: what pH do they need?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_007: ATP is made at the inner membrane by ATP synthase, not loose in the matrix. Check: where does the proton flow turn?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_008: Chlorophyll isn't one pigment — a, b and carotenoids each catch different light. Check: why does chromatography show bands?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_009: The envelope doesn't always dissolve — many fungi run a closed mitosis with it intact. Check: is every mitosis 'open'?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_010: Svedbergs don't add — 30S plus 50S makes 70S because shape counts, not just mass. Check: what does S measure?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_011: Don't trust the names — microtubules are the thickest (25 nm), microfilaments the thinnest (6). Check: which is 10 nm?
c11_biotech_cbse_02_012: Peroxisomes aren't lysosomes — they oxidise with catalase while lysosomes hydrolyse in acid. Check: which buds from the ER?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_001: D/L marks the C-5 configuration; alpha/beta marks the anomeric carbon — not rotation direction. Check: which carbon decides?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_002: The peptide bond links alpha-carboxyl to alpha-amino — never to an R-group. Check: which amino acid isn't chiral?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_003: Helix H-bonds run along the backbone, not between R-groups — and disulfides aren't 'secondary'. Check: which atoms hydrogen-bond?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_004: 'Lipid' is a solubility label, not a shape — the membrane is built from phospholipids, not triglycerides. Check: which lipid lines the cell?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_005: Not all steroids are hormones — cholesterol is mostly a membrane part and a precursor. Check: name a non-hormone steroid.
c11_biotech_cbse_03_006: The strands join by thousands of cooperative H-bonds plus stacking — weak singly, strong together. Check: what holds each strand internally?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_007: RNA isn't single-stranded DNA — its 2'-OH makes it fold, react and even catalyse. Check: what can rRNA do that DNA can't?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_008: 5' and 3' number the sugar's carbons, not the phosphate. Check: which carbon carries the free OH?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_009: Water resists heating because energy first breaks intermolecular H-bonds — not because it has three atoms. Check: which bond is ~20 kJ/mol?
c11_biotech_cbse_03_010: Vitamins don't give you calories — they're cofactors that let enzymes release energy. Check: is it fuel or a helper?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_001: Class an enzyme by the reaction it runs, not by its name — hexokinase is a transferase. Check: what bond chemistry happens?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_002: Even a 'lock and key' fit strains the substrate's bonds toward the transition state. Check: does the bound substrate stay unstrained?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_003: Induced fit isn't a floppy enzyme — the substrate stabilises a rare ready shape. Check: was the shape present before binding?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_004: Km isn't the same as Kd, and low Km isn't always better — compare kcat/Km. Check: what gives half Vmax?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_005: Heat doesn't make enzymes 'tired' — it unfolds them for good, and extreme pH can too. Check: does activity return on cooling?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_006: Km is the substrate level giving half Vmax — not the level for Vmax, and not always Kd. Check: what's v at [S] = Km?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_007: A pure non-competitive inhibitor drops Vmax but leaves Km alone — it binds E and ES equally. Check: does Km shift?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_008: An allosteric inhibitor can raise K0.5 while Vmax stays put — the sigmoid just slides right. Check: did the plateau drop?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_009: Cofactors and coenzymes differ — FAD comes from riboflavin (B2) and CoA from pantothenate (B5). Check: which vitamin makes FAD?
c11_biotech_cbse_04_010: Ribozymes aren't primitive leftovers — the ribosome's RNA core catalyses peptide bonds superbly. Check: what makes the peptide bond?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_001: 'Resting phase' is a misnomer — interphase is the busiest stretch, with its own checkpoints. Check: when does DNA double?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_002: After S phase you still have 46 chromosomes — each just carries two sister chromatids. Check: count centromeres, not chromatids.
c11_biotech_cbse_05_003: Fibres don't push chromosomes to the plate — kinetochores pull from both poles until tension balances. Check: what moves the chromosome?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_004: Mitosis adds cells; it doesn't enlarge them — and repair uses the same machinery. Check: hyperplasia or hypertrophy?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_005: Crossing over swaps non-sister chromatids of homologues — and no new S phase precedes meiosis II. Check: sisters or non-sisters?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_006: Meiosis II isn't plain mitosis — crossing over already made sisters different, so four gametes differ. Check: are sisters identical?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_007: Crossing over belongs to Prophase I and assortment to Metaphase I — homologues are gone by II. Check: are homologues still paired?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_008: Apoptosis is an orderly, ATP-driven shutdown — swelling, bursting and inflammation mean necrosis. Check: do caspases run?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_009: Apoptotic blebs are active remodelling — a necrotic cell swells and leaks instead. Check: is ATP still flowing?
c11_biotech_cbse_05_010: Cyclin binding alone doesn't switch a CDK on — it needs CAK's phosphate and Cdc25's cleanup. Check: is the T-loop phosphorylated?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_001: Mendel picked peas for control — selfing flowers, clear-cut traits and true-breeding lines. Check: could he force a cross?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_002: Dominant doesn't delete recessive — the allele hides in F1 and returns in F2. Check: can two talls give a dwarf?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_003: Segregation is homologues parting in meiosis I — a test cross gives 1:1 only for a heterozygote. Check: is the parent Tt or TT?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_004: 9:3:3:1 holds only for unlinked genes with full dominance — don't swap it with the genotypic ratio. Check: are the genes linked?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_005: Pink isn't roan — incomplete dominance blends, codominance shows both alleles fully. Check: one product halved or both present?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_006: Type AB isn't a blend — each red cell carries full A and full B antigens. Check: one antigen or two on the cell?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_007: Linked genes can still recombine — recombinants under 50% means linked, not zero. Check: what's the recombinant frequency?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_008: Sister chromatids are copies — swapping them changes nothing; only non-sisters carry different alleles. Check: can RF pass 50%?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_009: The Y isn't the universal male switch — a grasshopper male is simply XO, no Y at all. Check: which system does this species use?
c11_biotech_cbse_06_010: A skipped generation doesn't prove recessive — penetrance, carriers and X-linkage bend the pattern. Check: could it still be dominant?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_001: The Dogma only bans information flowing out of protein — RNA to DNA was never forbidden. Check: which arrow does it rule out?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_002: The coding strand isn't read — polymerase copies the template, and mRNA merely matches the coding. Check: which strand runs 3' to 5'?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_003: Pol II only builds the transcript — the cap and poly-A tail are added by separate enzymes. Check: who adds the tail?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_004: The cap isn't a normal link — it's a 5'-5' triphosphate bridge with N7-methyl on the guanine. Check: why can't exonucleases bite it?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_005: Introns aren't dead weight — they carry regulators, host small RNAs and enable alternative splicing. Check: what lives in an intron?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_006: Wobble covers many third-base changes, but not all — AGA codes Arg, not Ser. Check: is this codon family truly degenerate?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_007: The ribosome doesn't crawl 3' to 5' — the mRNA threads through so codons enter 5' to 3'. Check: which codon enters the A site next?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_008: Peptide bonds are made by rRNA, not a protein — powered by the aminoacyl-tRNA ester. Check: what does GTP drive instead?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_009: PTMs aren't just on-off switches — they combine into codes and some are structural must-haves. Check: regulatory or structural?
c11_biotech_cbse_07_010: Lactose never touches the operator — it reshapes the repressor so the repressor lets go. Check: what does the inducer bind?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_001: No normal human chromosome is truly telocentric — acrocentrics still carry a short arm with satellites. Check: is a p arm visible?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_002: A karyotype can't spot a one-gene disease — each band hides millions of bases. Check: is the lesion band-sized?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_003: 2n+1 means 47 chromosomes total — and unlike trisomy, full polyploidy almost never reaches birth. Check: what does 2n equal?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_004: 'No DNA lost' doesn't mean harmless — a break can split a gene or strand it away from its enhancer. Check: where did the breaks land?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_005: Lost acrocentric p-arms aren't a tragedy — they held only redundant rRNA repeats. Check: are those genes multicopy?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_006: Down syndrome usually isn't inherited — it's fresh non-disjunction, not a family trait. Check: what's the real recurrence risk?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_007: Klinefelter is an extra X, not an extra Y — and Turner's missing X often comes from the father. Check: which nondisjunction happened?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_008: Dominant doesn't mean common — it describes expression in a heterozygote, not population frequency. Check: how frequent is Huntington's?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_009: A carrier female can still show symptoms — random X-inactivation leaves some cells mutant. Check: which X is active in her cells?
c11_biotech_cbse_08_010: The mutation doesn't draw a sickle — HbS polymerises only when oxygen drops. Check: what triggers the shape change?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_001: Bioinformatics isn't just running BLAST — it's a pipeline from quality control to assembly. Check: what step feeds your search?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_002: Sort databases by provenance, not molecule — UniProt is curated from GenBank, not primary. Check: who submitted the data?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_003: The three banks mirror the same records daily — only the accession labels differ. Check: which namespace are you searching?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_004: A PDB file is more than coordinates — the header tells you the method, mutants and ligands. Check: is it wild-type?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_005: GenBank is a strict flat-file format — and don't swap FASTA's '>' for FASTQ's '@'. Check: does the file carry quality scores?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_006: Global vs local is about scope, not similarity — use global for full-length comparison. Check: whole protein or a domain?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_007: In traceback, follow the move that made the cell — not just the biggest neighbour. Check: where did F(i,j) come from?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_008: BLOSUM numbers run opposite to PAM — higher BLOSUM means closer kin, higher PAM means farther. Check: which matrix for distant kin?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_009: A low E-value isn't just high identity — alignment length and database size bend it. Check: how long is the match?
c11_biotech_cbse_09_010: Parsimony can be fooled by long branches, and 95% bootstrap means repeatable — not 95% true. Check: are branch rates unequal?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_001: One PDB entry can hold several CATH domains — and H means structural kinship, not sequence. Check: how many domains in the chain?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_002: A high instability index means *less* stable — and positive GRAVY means hydrophobic. Check: which way do the signs run?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_003: Chou-Fasman gives a 1D string of H, E and C — no coordinates, no 3D model. Check: does it output phi/psi angles?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_004: Percent identity isn't a quality score — coverage and template resolution matter just as much. Check: how much got modelled?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_005: Threading still uses a template — only ab initio folds from scratch. Check: is a fold match detectable at all?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_006: 'Allowed' on a Ramachandran plot means no steric clash — not that it's energetically happy. Check: does it count H-bonds?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_007: PyMOL tracks objects and selections; RasMol just draws — commands behave differently. Check: is 'hide' global or per-selection?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_008: Docking isn't the main PPI predictor — most confident pairs come from interologs and networks. Check: was a candidate found first?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_009: A 40%-identical hit can still do a different job — paralogs diverge in specificity. Check: ortholog or paralog?
c11_biotech_cbse_10_010: A template isn't copy-paste — loops drift and side chains repack even at 40% identity. Check: did the loops get remodelled?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_001: You won't be inventing algorithms — most bioinformatics code glues libraries and parses files. Check: can Biopython already do it?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_002: You don't need all of Python — strings, files, dicts and Biopython cover most tasks. Check: have you parsed a real FASTA yet?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_003: SeqIO.parse gives you an iterator — you can't index it or len() it. Check: did you mean SeqIO.read or list()?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_004: A dot won't cross a newline unless you add the s flag — wrapped FASTA will silently fail. Check: does your regex span lines?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_005: RStudio is just the editor — base R does the work, and unsaved console lines aren't reproducible. Check: is it in a script?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_006: Don't split FASTA on newlines — wrapped lines and edge cases will bite you; use a real parser. Check: is the sequence wrapped?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_007: translate() won't hunt for ATG — it reads from the first base in the frame you gave. Check: did you set the frame yourself?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_008: In a global alignment, traceback always starts at the bottom-right corner — the ends must align. Check: where did you start?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_009: Splitting on '>' breaks on stray characters, CRLF and giant files — parse line by line. Check: did a \r sneak in?
c11_biotech_cbse_11_010: A package call is still a web request — set your email and API key or you'll get throttled. Check: is Entrez.email set?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_001: More zoom isn't more detail — resolution sets the limit, and light stops near 200 nm. Check: can it resolve 20 nm?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_002: RPM isn't g-force — rotor size matters, and differential spins sort by sedimentation rate, not density. Check: what RCF did you use?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_003: Beer-Lambert bends at high absorbance — and molar epsilon isn't the per-gram coefficient. Check: is A above ~1?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_004: Shape, not just mass, sets elution in gel filtration — and a cation exchanger binds positive proteins. Check: what's the resin's charge?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_005: Taq doesn't copy the whole genome — only the stretch between your two primers grows exponentially. Check: where do primers bind?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_006: DNA's charge grows with its mass, so the gel sieves by size alone — small fragments win. Check: is charge-to-mass constant?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_007: Two 5' overhangs only ligate if the sequences match — AATT won't anneal to GATC. Check: do the overhangs complement?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_008: Antibiotic selection proves the plasmid entered — not that it carries your insert. Check: how big is the fragment?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_009: The blot is the transfer to membrane, not the stain — Southern is DNA, Northern RNA, Western protein. Check: what was probed?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_010: ddNTPs are diluted in — each molecule stops at a random base, building a full ladder. Check: do fragments end at every position?
c11_biotech_cbse_12_011: Serum-free doesn't mean factor-free — and auxin-cytokinin recipes differ by species. Check: which growth factors remain required?
c11_bs_cbse_01_001: Ancient Indian trade wasn't all barter — hundis and coinage ran real credit networks. Check: what instrument paid the supplier?
c11_bs_cbse_01_002: A salaried engineer isn't a 'professional' — no independent practice, capital or professional body. Check: whose code governs them?
c11_bs_cbse_01_003: One profitable sale isn't business — it takes regular dealing plus risk and uncertainty. Check: was it a one-off disposal?
c11_bs_cbse_01_004: Tertiary and commerce overlap but aren't the same — a doctor's service is a profession, not commerce. Check: nature or function?
c11_bs_cbse_01_005: Farming isn't extractive — breeding and raising living things makes it a genetic industry. Check: is anything reproduced or reared?
c11_bs_cbse_01_006: Each auxiliary kills one hindrance — warehousing beats time, transport beats place. Check: which hindrance does this remove?
c11_bs_cbse_01_007: Wholesale means selling to resellers, not selling big — a consumer buying 1,000 units is still retail. Check: who's the buyer?
c11_bs_cbse_01_008: Trade itself only removes the hindrance of person — moving goods is transport's job. Check: ownership change or physical move?
c11_bs_cbse_01_009: Social responsibility isn't donating profits — it's running the business desirably, and profit funds it. Check: obligation or charity?
c11_bs_cbse_01_010: Business risk isn't a computed probability — it's the uncertainty built into operations. Check: cause of risk or a number?
c11_bs_cbse_01_011: Profit maximisation means a fair return, not profit at any cost — and service walks beside it. Check: reasonable or unlimited?
c11_bs_cbse_02_001: Unlimited liability is the owner's problem — creditors can reach personal assets beyond the firm. Check: whose assets are exposed?
c11_bs_cbse_02_002: A Karta isn't a managing partner — the role comes by birth, can't be voted out, and stays unlimited. Check: agreement or birth?
c11_bs_cbse_02_003: A partnership exists by agreement alone — registration is optional but blocks the firm's own suits. Check: can it sue outsiders?
c11_bs_cbse_02_004: A nominal partner is liable to outsiders in full, whatever the internal deal. Check: did third parties rely on the name?
c11_bs_cbse_02_005: The Act always applies — the deed just overrides defaults, and silence triggers the statute. Check: what does the deed say on drawings?
c11_bs_cbse_02_006: An unregistered firm isn't illegal — it can be sued freely but can't sue back. Check: which direction is barred?
c11_bs_cbse_02_007: Cooperative types follow the members' purpose — Amul is a producers' co-op, not consumers'. Check: who are the members?
c11_bs_cbse_02_008: Limited liability caps at the unpaid share amount — fully paid means zero, but fraud can pierce it. Check: are shares fully paid?
c11_bs_cbse_02_009: An OPC isn't just a one-member private company — one director, no AGM, and a nominee are its own rules. Check: how many directors?
c11_bs_cbse_02_010: There's no one best form — the right choice shifts with scale, capital need and stage. Check: what suits the business now?
c11_bs_cbse_02_011: Sharing losses doesn't cap liability — any one partner can be made to pay it all. Check: joint and several?
c11_bs_cbse_03_001: 'Public limited' is about share trading; 'public sector' is about who owns 51%+. Check: who holds the shares?
c11_bs_cbse_03_002: Not every government department is an undertaking — only ones selling goods or services, like Railways. Check: does it earn revenue?
c11_bs_cbse_03_003: A statutory corporation is its own creature — born of a special Act, with its own staff and finances. Check: which law created it?
c11_bs_cbse_03_004: Government shares alone don't make a government company — the 51% threshold must be crossed. Check: what's the exact holding?
c11_bs_cbse_03_005: A government company still answers to its majority owner — the government appoints directors and policy. Check: who appoints the board?
c11_bs_cbse_03_006: Selling 10% isn't privatisation — disinvestment can keep 51% control intact. Check: did management control change hands?
c11_bs_cbse_03_007: A JV doesn't merge the parents — they stay independent and only share the venture. Check: did any company cease to exist?
c11_bs_cbse_03_008: Exporting to India doesn't make a firm an MNC — it needs operations in multiple countries under one control. Check: does it produce abroad?
c11_bs_cbse_03_009: FDI size isn't the whole story — check sourcing, profit repatriation and technology spillover. Check: how much stays in India?
c11_bs_cbse_03_010: A public limited company belongs to its shareholders — 'public' means open shareholding, not government. Check: who owns it?
c11_bs_cbse_04_001: Business services are the five enablers — banking, insurance, transport, warehousing, communication. Check: does it enable the core?
c11_bs_cbse_04_002: An RD isn't a monthly FD — each instalment earns interest for a different stretch. Check: how long did the last deposit earn?
c11_bs_cbse_04_003: A demand draft is already paid — the bank owes the payee, so you can't stop it like a cheque. Check: who holds the obligation?
c11_bs_cbse_04_004: Utmost good faith mainly binds you, the proposer — the insurer needn't reveal its underwriting. Check: who knows the risk facts?
c11_bs_cbse_04_005: Contribution is the insurers' affair — you can't pick one to pay all, and recovery caps at the loss. Check: can you claim twice?
c11_bs_cbse_04_006: Indemnity pays your actual loss, not the policy amount — ₹6L loss on a ₹10L policy pays ₹6L. Check: loss or sum insured?
c11_bs_cbse_04_007: Theft isn't one policy — it sits inside burglary, motor and household covers. Check: which policy carries the peril?
c11_bs_cbse_04_008: Telecom isn't just mobiles and posts aren't just letters — VSAT and postal finance count too. Check: does the post office sell PPF?
c11_bs_cbse_04_009: Fastest or cheapest isn't 'best' — match the mode to the goods, distance and urgency. Check: is coal worth air freight?
c11_bs_cbse_04_010: A bonded warehouse holds duty-unpaid imports in bond — public warehouses hold cleared goods. Check: has duty been paid?
c11_bs_cbse_05_001: E-business isn't just online shopping — internal digital processes and B2B count too. Check: is the factory networked inside?
c11_bs_cbse_05_002: E-business isn't only for giants — the net lowers entry barriers, and the hurdles are human too. Check: what resistance is human?
c11_bs_cbse_05_003: A firm isn't 'a B2C company' — the same business runs B2B, B2C and intra-B at once. Check: which transaction is this?
c11_bs_cbse_05_004: No storefront doesn't mean no infrastructure — warehouses, logistics and servers still run behind. Check: who fulfils the order?
c11_bs_cbse_05_005: Digital cash is prepaid value stored on your device — net-banking moves money live during the sale. Check: is the bank in the loop?
c11_bs_cbse_05_006: Outsourcing isn't only offshoring — a local laundry contract for a hospital counts too. Check: is it non-core and external?
c11_bs_cbse_05_007: BPO isn't only call centres — legal and research work count, and a captive unit abroad still offshores. Check: owned or contracted?
c11_bs_cbse_05_008: Outsourcing is about focus, not just cheap wages — a same-city payroll contract qualifies. Check: core or non-core activity?
c11_bs_cbse_05_009: These aren't all 'online buying' — procurement auctions inputs, e-trading moves financial assets. Check: what's being exchanged?
c11_bs_cbse_05_010: Data isn't just your catalogue — transactions, supplier feeds and compliance records are data too. Check: what does GST filing need?
c11_bs_cbse_06_001: Social responsibility isn't charity — fair wages and clean processes are obligations, not gifts. Check: duty or donation?
c11_bs_cbse_06_002: The arguments aren't preaching — each shows how business resources solve social problems better. Check: what's the causal link?
c11_bs_cbse_06_003: The 'against' list is critics' theory, not real behaviour — the 'reality' forces explain actual compliance. Check: theory or practice?
c11_bs_cbse_06_004: Shareholders get a fair return on a safe investment — not maximum dividends at any cost. Check: short-term or sustainable?
c11_bs_cbse_06_005: Ethics isn't CSR or mere legality — it's the moral code behind operations. Check: is it an element or an activity?
c11_bs_cbse_06_006: Donations can't launder a rotten core — ethical responsibility runs through daily operations. Check: ethical or discretionary?
c11_bs_cbse_06_007: Obeying the law is the floor, not the fulfilment — responsibility asks for voluntary fairness beyond it. Check: legal floor or ethical ask?
c11_bs_cbse_06_008: CSR isn't optional kindness — thresholds make it mandatory and staff welfare doesn't count. Check: is the spend statutory?
c11_bs_cbse_06_009: Unfair trade practice has no size exemption — a street vendor's hollow measure counts too. Check: does scale matter?
c11_bs_cbse_06_010: Protection isn't just filters at the pipe's end — redesigning the process prevents pollution at source. Check: treat or prevent?
c11_bs_cbse_07_001: A paid CA drafting documents isn't a promoter — promotion is a legal status with fiduciary duties. Check: was it for a fee?
c11_bs_cbse_07_002: Promoters don't automatically own or direct — and pre-incorporation contracts can never be ratified. Check: did the company exist yet?
c11_bs_cbse_07_003: Incorporation is birth, not permission to trade — and the registrar checks form, not truth. Check: can the company start business yet?
c11_bs_cbse_07_004: The MoA isn't as flexible as the Articles — object changes need more, and ultra vires acts can't be saved. Check: which document governs?
c11_bs_cbse_07_005: 'Subsidiary' doesn't mean ignorable — the Articles bind like a contract and need a special resolution. Check: which resolution type?
c11_bs_cbse_07_006: Incorporation gives birth; commencement gives permission — the certificate shields the fact, not illegal acts. Check: which permits trading?
c11_bs_cbse_07_007: Hitting minimum subscription isn't enough — allotment also needs listing, and 90% is of the issue size. Check: which 90%?
c11_bs_cbse_07_008: The commencement certificate isn't public-only — both company types need it within 180 days. Check: public or private?
c11_bs_cbse_07_009: A company can't ratify what was signed before it existed — there was no principal then. Check: when was it signed?
c11_bs_cbse_07_010: Ultra vires the Articles can still be ratified — only acts beyond the Memorandum are dead. Check: which document was exceeded?
c11_bs_cbse_08_001: Finance isn't just bank loans — equity and retained profits count, and one source fits several lenses. Check: borrowed or owned?
c11_bs_cbse_08_002: Long-term doesn't mean owner's — debentures are long-term and borrowed. Check: which two axes apply?
c11_bs_cbse_08_003: Fixed dividend doesn't make preference shares debt — they're still owner's capital. Check: share or loan?
c11_bs_cbse_08_004: No compulsory dividend doesn't mean free — equity carries the highest expected return. Check: what's the cost of equity?
c11_bs_cbse_08_005: Preference dividend isn't a charge on profits — it's an appropriation, and they can't sue for it. Check: is profit even available?
c11_bs_cbse_08_006: Debentures aren't just bank loans — they can be unsecured, convertible and tradable. Check: is there always collateral?
