c11_bs_cbse_08_007: Retained earnings aren't free — shareholders' expected return is the real cost. Check: does 12% beat their required 15%?
c11_bs_cbse_08_008: 'No interest' trade credit can hide ~37% a year if you skip the early-payment discount. Check: what discount did you forgo?
c11_bs_cbse_08_009: Banks lend short from deposits; development institutions fund long projects — not interchangeable. Check: asset life or liability term?
c11_bs_cbse_08_010: A lease never makes you the owner — hire purchase does when the last instalment clears. Check: bailment or agreement to sell?
c11_bs_cbse_08_011: The cheapest-looking source can hide costs — lost discounts, opportunity cost, supplier limits. Check: what's the hidden price?
c11_bs_cbse_09_001: Both investment and turnover must fit the class — it lands in the highest where both hold. Check: do both limits pass?
c11_bs_cbse_09_002: MSMEs aren't just mini-factories — they run where big industry can't, balancing regions. Check: jobs or also location?
c11_bs_cbse_09_003: The seven MSME problems chain together — tight finance ripples into weak marketing and back. Check: which problem causes the next?
c11_bs_cbse_09_004: Not every scheme hands out money — some guarantee loans, some refinance, some create demand. Check: what instrument is it?
c11_bs_cbse_09_005: Entrepreneurial risk is calculated — odds assessed and tilted by skill, not a lottery ticket. Check: can the odds be estimated?
c11_bs_cbse_09_006: A hired CEO isn't an entrepreneur — no personal risk, no uncertainty ownership. Check: who bears the failure?
c11_bs_cbse_09_007: An EDP isn't only for ready founders — it builds the person before the idea. Check: did they start with a plan?
c11_bs_cbse_09_008: The type labels stack — one entrepreneur can be technical, small, urban and innovative at once. Check: which axes all apply?
c11_bs_cbse_09_009: Development isn't just 'more GDP' — trace the mechanism: savings, innovation, regional spread. Check: risk or uncertainty?
c11_bs_cbse_09_010: A tax holiday is temporary and covers only income tax — not GST or TDS. Check: which taxes still apply?
c11_bs_cbse_10_001: Internal trade means within the nation — Delhi to Mumbai is still internal. Check: did a national border get crossed?
c11_bs_cbse_10_002: Breaking bulk is dividing quantity — grading sorts by quality. Check: did you split kilos or sort them?
c11_bs_cbse_10_003: A huge hypermarket selling to households is still retail — the buyer's identity decides, not shop size. Check: who's the end buyer?
c11_bs_cbse_10_004: Street traders have no fixed structure; stall holders do — same street, different category. Check: is there a fixed stall?
c11_bs_cbse_10_005: A big village store is still small-scale — it's the structure, like chains and centralised buying, that counts. Check: who does the buying?
c11_bs_cbse_10_006: A departmental store is centralised buying, decentralised sales, full service — not a supermarket. Check: self-service or served?
c11_bs_cbse_10_007: Chain stores sell one narrow range across many branches — wide variety makes it a departmental store. Check: one line or many?

c11_chem_cbse_04_009: In O₂ the topmost electrons sit in π* — O₂⁺ loses one of those. Check: which orbital is the HOMO?
c11_chem_cbse_04_010: H–Cl doesn't hydrogen-bond — only N, O and F carry enough charge density. Check: who is H bonded to?

c11_chem_cbse_04_012: Polar bonds can cancel out — and in NF₃ the lone-pair dipole fights the bond dipoles. Check: do the vectors cancel?
c11_chem_cbse_05_001: Van der Waals covers more than London forces — dipole-dipole counts, but H-bonds sit above them all. Check: how strong is it?
c11_chem_cbse_05_002: London forces act in every molecule, polar or not — and shape can beat molar mass. Check: linear or branched?
c11_chem_cbse_05_003: Electronegativity alone isn't enough — H-bonding needs the small size of N, O or F. Check: is the atom too big?

c11_chem_cbse_05_005: Celsius breaks the gas laws — convert to kelvin before you take ratios. Check: did you add 273?

c11_chem_cbse_05_007: On mixing, each gas expands into the full volume — recompute each partial pressure. Check: did you apply Boyle per gas?
c11_chem_cbse_05_008: Graham's law carries a square root — rate ratio is √(M₂/M₁). Check: diffusion through gas or a pinhole?
c11_chem_cbse_05_009: Three speeds, three formulas — Graham's uses the average, the gas equation needs rms. Check: which speed does yours want?
c11_chem_cbse_05_010: Ideal behaviour fails at low temperature too — and at extreme pressure Z can top 1. Check: attraction or volume?
c11_chem_cbse_05_011: The correction adds to measured P and subtracts from measured V — not the reverse. Check: which sign went where?

c11_chem_cbse_06_002: Use ΔU = q + w — expansion work comes out negative. Check: what's w's sign?

c11_chem_cbse_06_004: Formation equations build one mole of compound — and combustion ends at liquid water. Check: one mole of what?
c11_chem_cbse_06_005: Elements score zero only in their standard state — ozone and diamond don't qualify. Check: which allotrope?
c11_chem_cbse_06_006: Bond enthalpies are averages, and the broken-minus-formed trick needs gases. Check: all species gaseous?
c11_chem_cbse_06_007: Negative ΔG° doesn't mean total conversion — at equilibrium ΔG is zero, not the reactants. Check: ΔG or ΔG°?
c11_chem_cbse_06_008: q/T only counts on a reversible path — irreversible trips need a detour. Check: which path are you on?
c11_chem_cbse_06_009: Zero entropy needs a perfect crystal — frozen CO keeps residual entropy from random orientations. Check: is it perfect?
c11_chem_cbse_06_010: Only ΔG° ties to K — at equilibrium ΔG itself is zero. Check: are you at equilibrium?
c11_chem_cbse_07_001: Equilibrium isn't stillness — evaporation and condensation keep trading blows. Check: are the rates equal?
c11_chem_cbse_07_002: Equal rates don't mean equal amounts — equilibrium can sit at 85% product. Check: rates or concentrations?
c11_chem_cbse_07_003: Pure solids and liquids don't enter K — their activity is one. Check: did CaCO₃ sneak in?
c11_chem_cbse_07_004: Only gases count in Δn_g — and match R to your pressure units. Check: bar or atm?
c11_chem_cbse_07_005: In Q and K the coefficients become powers — 3H₂ means [H₂]³. Check: exponents or multipliers?
c11_chem_cbse_07_006: Adding a reactant shifts forward but never fully undoes it — the new level stays higher. Check: higher than original?
c11_chem_cbse_07_007: Pressure moves the position, never the constant — Kp holds at fixed T. Check: did Kp really change?
c11_chem_cbse_07_008: A catalyst quickens both directions equally — you reach the same yield sooner. Check: does K move?
c11_chem_cbse_07_009: A Bronsted base just accepts a proton — NH₃ qualifies without any OH. Check: who accepted H⁺?
c11_chem_cbse_07_010: Lewis acids aren't only octet-poor — cations and polar double bonds accept pairs too. Check: who accepts the pair?
c11_chem_cbse_07_011: Water stays out of Kb — its activity is one, so drop [H₂O]. Check: what are the units?
c11_chem_cbse_07_012: 10⁻⁸ M HCl can't give pH 8 — water's own ions matter. Check: did you count water's H⁺?
c11_chem_cbse_07_013: A buffer needs a weak partner — HCl plus NaCl won't buffer. Check: is the acid weak?
c11_chem_cbse_07_014: For Ag₂CrO₄ the silver term is squared — and a common ion starts at its added level. Check: where did Cl⁻ begin?
c11_chem_cbse_07_015: Write hydrolysis with the ion, not the salt — NH₄⁺ donates a proton to water. Check: which ion reacts?

c11_chem_cbse_08_007: Disproportionation needs one element going both ways — KClO₃ only reduces Cl. Check: does the same element rise and fall?
c11_chem_cbse_08_008: Each Cr gains three electrons, but there are two — the n-factor is 6, not 3. Check: M/3 or M/6?

c11_chem_cbse_09_003: Copper won't fizz in dilute acid — check the reactivity series first. Check: is the metal above H?
c11_chem_cbse_09_004: N₂ + H₂ doesn't just run at STP — Haber needs heat, pressure and a catalyst. Check: what conditions are stated?
c11_chem_cbse_09_005: One triglyceride carries three double bonds — hydrogenation takes three H₂, not one. Check: how many C=C per molecule?
c11_chem_cbse_09_006: Metallic hydrides aren't fixed formulas — hydrogen just parks in lattice gaps. Check: stoichiometric or interstitial?
c11_chem_cbse_09_007: Water isn't linear — two lone pairs bend it, and the proton never floats naked: it's H₃O⁺. Check: how many domains on O?
c11_chem_cbse_09_008: Hardness isn't just 'lots of solids' — only bicarbonates boil away; chlorides stay. Check: which anion is it?
c11_chem_cbse_09_009: Clark's method calls for quicklime, CaO — not slaked lime. Check: which lime did you write?
c11_chem_cbse_09_010: Heavy water isn't radioactive — that's tritiated water; D₂O is stable. Check: which isotope is in it?
c11_chem_cbse_09_011: Oxygen in peroxide is −1, not −2 — and concentrated H₂O₂ is less stable, not more. Check: what's O's state?

c11_cs_cbse_01_011: In hex, A to F are digits worth 10 to 15 — not unknowns to solve for. Check: what is A worth?
c11_cs_cbse_01_012: Read remainders bottom-up and group bits from the right — the direction matters. Check: which end is the LSB?
c11_cs_cbse_01_013: In binary a borrow brings in 10₂ — that's two, not ten. Check: did a 9 sneak in?

c11_cs_cbse_02_001: In Boolean algebra 1 + 1 is 1 — OR isn't addition. Check: true OR true?
c11_cs_cbse_02_002: 0 and 1 are truth states here, not integers — A + A stays A. Check: logical or numeric?
c11_cs_cbse_02_003: NOT binds tightest, then AND, then OR — and OR includes 'both'. Check: did the brackets move?

c11_cs_cbse_03_004: A formula isn't an algorithm — you need Start, Input, actions and Stop. Check: where's the assignment?

c11_cs_cbse_03_006: A diamond asks one yes/no question — four-way menus need nested diamonds. Check: how many arrows leave it?
c11_cs_cbse_03_007: Pseudocode isn't sloppy Python — use INPUT, OUTPUT, END IF. Check: could a non-coder read it?
c11_cs_cbse_03_008: Ladder conditions run top-down — a 95 grabs 'B' if 75 is checked first. Check: which condition fires first?
c11_cs_cbse_03_009: A while checks before every run — once i hits 11 the body never executes. Check: is it tested first?

c11_cs_cbse_03_011: Listing steps isn't decomposition — split into independent sub-problems with their own I/O. Check: can each be tested alone?
c11_cs_cbse_03_012: O(n) isn't n seconds — it's growth rate, and input space doesn't count as extra. Check: auxiliary or input memory?
c11_cs_cbse_04_001: Interpreted doesn't mean weak — Python refuses '2' + 3. Check: dynamic or weak typing?
c11_cs_cbse_04_002: The IDLE Shell forgets everything on close — write programs in the Editor. Check: where's your file saved?

c11_cs_cbse_04_005: 'If' is a legal identifier — but it will haunt you later; avoid keyword lookalikes. Check: readable or risky?
c11_cs_cbse_04_006: Triple quotes make a string literal, not a comment — only # is discarded. Check: does it reach bytecode?

c11_cs_cbse_04_010: s = 'world' didn't change 'hello' — the name was rebound. Check: object changed or name moved?
c11_cs_cbse_04_011: * and / share precedence and run left to right — 20/5*2 is 8. Check: which pairs share a tier?

c11_cs_cbse_04_013: No red error doesn't mean right — test against a known value like 32°F → 0°C. Check: what's your test case?
c11_cs_cbse_04_014: Random prints bury the bug — trace selected values through a dry run. Check: which line actually broke it?
c11_cs_cbse_05_001: A while doesn't watch mid-body — it finishes the iteration, then re-checks. Check: when is the test run?
c11_cs_cbse_05_002: '10' > 2 throws a TypeError in Python — and a < b < c chains, not nests. Check: are the types compatible?
c11_cs_cbse_05_003: Python doesn't need parentheses around the condition — and '=' won't fly inside if. Check: assign or compare?

c11_cs_cbse_05_006: The ternary picks a value — it's an expression, not a mini statement block. Check: what does it return?
c11_cs_cbse_05_007: A while can run zero times — the condition is tested before the body. Check: was it ever true?
c11_cs_cbse_05_008: The condition is tested at the top of each round — a mid-body change won't stop it early. Check: did the body finish?
c11_cs_cbse_05_009: range() doesn't build a list — it's a lazy sequence that yields on demand. Check: will range(10⁹) eat RAM?

c11_cs_cbse_05_011: break frees only the innermost loop — the outer one keeps going. Check: which loop did it exit?
c11_cs_cbse_05_012: A loop's else runs whenever break didn't fire — even after zero iterations. Check: was break hit?
c11_cs_cbse_05_013: A for can run forever — append to the list you're looping over and see. Check: is the sequence mutating?
c11_cs_cbse_06_001: Python has no char type — 'a' and "a" are both length-1 strings. Check: does len('a') work?
c11_cs_cbse_06_002: The first character sits at index 0 — the index is an offset, not an ordinal. Check: what's s[len(s)]?
c11_cs_cbse_06_003: The stop index is exclusive — and negative indices don't reverse without a negative step. Check: what did s[-1:-4] give?
c11_cs_cbse_06_004: s + 'x' builds a new string — the old one never changed. Check: same object or rebound name?
c11_cs_cbse_06_005: s.upper() returns a new string — the original stays lowercase. Check: did you assign the result?
c11_cs_cbse_06_006: In 'for ch in s', the variable holds each character — not its index. Check: value or position?
c11_cs_cbse_06_007: Reusing the name isn't mutation — s.upper() alone leaves s untouched. Check: did you reassign?
c11_cs_cbse_06_008: Python lists hold any objects — mixing ints and strings is legal. Check: references or raw values?
c11_cs_cbse_06_009: Index counts steps from the start — [0] is first and [-1] is last. Check: what is lst[-len(lst)]?
c11_cs_cbse_06_010: Slicing copies; it doesn't cut the original — and lst * 0.5 just errors. Check: is it an int multiplier?
c11_cs_cbse_06_011: append and friends return None — and remove() hunts a value while pop() takes an index. Check: value or position?
c11_cs_cbse_06_012: 'for row in matrix' hands you each inner list — not an index. Check: what is row?
c11_cs_cbse_06_013: In a comprehension the 'if' filters the items first — the expression runs after. Check: what's being tested?
c11_cs_cbse_06_014: A slice copy is shallow — nested lists inside still point at the same objects. Check: did the inner list change too?
c11_cs_cbse_07_001: A tuple locks its references, not the objects — a list inside can still grow. Check: container or contents?
c11_cs_cbse_07_002: Commas make the tuple — (5) is just an int, but (5,) is a tuple. Check: where's the comma?
c11_cs_cbse_07_003: t + u builds a fresh tuple — nothing mutates. Check: same object or new?
c11_cs_cbse_07_004: index(v, start, end) reports the position in the whole tuple — not in the slice. Check: 3 or 1?
c11_cs_cbse_07_005: Appending to a list inside a tuple is allowed — the tuple's references never moved. Check: what actually changed?
c11_cs_cbse_07_006: The left side is a pattern of targets, not a tuple — and the right must be iterable. Check: can you unpack an int?
c11_cs_cbse_07_007: Dict keys must be hashable — a list can't be one. Check: could its contents change?
c11_cs_cbse_07_008: d[0] hunts for a key literally equal to 0 — insertion order doesn't give positions. Check: key or index?
c11_cs_cbse_07_009: d[key] = v silently overwrites — and pop() hands the value back. Check: did the key already exist?
c11_cs_cbse_07_010: keys() gives a live view, not a list — and get() saves you from KeyError. Check: is it subscriptable?
c11_cs_cbse_07_011: Looping a dict yields keys — and resizing it mid-loop throws RuntimeError. Check: adding keys inside the loop?
c11_cs_cbse_07_012: marks[101] won't spring into existence — nested dicts need explicit creation. Check: which level raised KeyError?
c11_cs_cbse_07_013: dict() won't pair neighbours — each element must already be a (key, value) pair. Check: what shape are the items?
c11_cs_cbse_08_001: Functions aren't just for repeated code — they package intent even when called once. Check: does the name say what it does?
c11_cs_cbse_08_002: 'def' only builds the function — nothing runs until you call it with (). Check: definition or invocation?
c11_cs_cbse_08_003: print shows a value; return hands it back — without return you get None. Check: what did the caller receive?
c11_cs_cbse_08_004: Positions bind arguments, not the names — power(2, 3) means base 2. Check: which slot did each value fill?
c11_cs_cbse_08_005: Defaults must trail the required ones — and a default list is shared across calls. Check: was the list recreated?
c11_cs_cbse_08_006: Once you use a keyword, the rest must be keywords too — position matters until then. Check: where did = first appear?
c11_cs_cbse_08_007: It's the asterisks that matter — *args and **kwargs are just conventional names. Check: what does the * do?
c11_cs_cbse_08_008: Assigning inside a function makes that name local everywhere in it — use global to write. Check: did UnboundLocalError bite?
c11_cs_cbse_08_009: Reading a global needs no declaration — 'global' only matters when you assign. Check: are you writing to it?
c11_cs_cbse_08_010: return a, b, c hands back one tuple — unpack or index it on the other side. Check: one object or three?
c11_cs_cbse_08_011: Recursion must shrink toward a base case — self-calls alone just spin. Check: does each call get simpler?
c11_cs_cbse_08_012: A lambda holds one expression — no loops, no statements. Check: can it be written as one expression?
c11_cs_cbse_08_013: from math import * brings the names in — not the module itself, so math.sqrt fails. Check: is 'math' defined?
c11_cs_cbse_08_014: Re-importing doesn't re-run the module — Python caches it in sys.modules. Check: did top-level code re-execute?
c11_cs_cbse_09_001: Renaming a .jpg to .txt doesn't make it text — the bytes inside decide. Check: what does the content look like?
c11_cs_cbse_09_002: open() only connects — call read() to pull the data. Check: is f a string or a handle?
c11_cs_cbse_09_003: 'w' wipes the file first — it never appends. Check: what happened to the old content?
c11_cs_cbse_09_004: readline() keeps the trailing newline — unlike input(). Check: did len() count it?
c11_cs_cbse_09_005: write() adds nothing — no newline, and writelines() doesn't separate either. Check: where's your newline?
c11_cs_cbse_09_006: Don't rely on the program ending — an unflushed buffer or exception can lose data. Check: is close() in a finally?
c11_cs_cbse_09_007: After the with-block, f exists but is closed. Check: f.closed — true or false?
c11_cs_cbse_09_008: In text mode, positions are bytes, not characters — arbitrary seek can land mid-encoding. Check: chars or bytes?
c11_cs_cbse_09_009: In append mode every write jumps to the end — seek(0) won't let you overwrite. Check: where did it land?
c11_cs_cbse_09_010: Binary mode wants bytes — 'wb' won't take a str, and pickles aren't readable text. Check: str or bytes?
c11_cs_cbse_09_011: A bare except hides everything — catch the specific error and close the file in finally. Check: does 'w' create the file?
c11_cs_cbse_09_012: Concatenating files can glue words together — and split() only breaks on whitespace. Check: did 'endstart' appear?
c11_cs_cbse_10_001: A list used wrong isn't a stack — insert(0, x) is O(n) and breaks the contract. Check: which end is the top?
c11_cs_cbse_10_002: A stack forbids indexing and mid-inserts — the list underneath is just storage. Check: is only the top reachable?
c11_cs_cbse_10_003: pop() removes as it returns — and top marks the last element, not the next slot. Check: did the stack shrink?
c11_cs_cbse_10_004: A bare list won't stop you sorting or inserting mid-way — wrap it to enforce LIFO. Check: what stops a mid-insert?
c11_cs_cbse_10_005: A deque stacks with append() and pop() — the 'left' methods serve queues. Check: which end is the top?
c11_cs_cbse_10_006: peek reads the top; pop removes it — choose carefully. Check: did the data survive?
c11_cs_cbse_10_007: An empty stack isn't proof — each pop must match the closing bracket's type. Check: did ([)] pass wrongly?
c11_cs_cbse_10_008: Exponentiation groups right — A^B^C is A^(B^C), so postfix is A B C ^ ^. Check: which way does ^ lean?
c11_cs_cbse_10_009: In a queue the front is where people leave — newcomers join the rear. Check: which end deletes?
c11_cs_cbse_10_010: Rear points at the next empty slot — insert there, delete at front. Check: where does enqueue write?
c11_cs_cbse_10_011: pop(0) shifts every element left — it's O(n), not O(1). Check: how many items moved?
c11_cs_cbse_10_012: For a queue on deque, append right and popleft — not pop. Check: which method dequeues?
c11_cs_cbse_10_013: front == rear can't mean both full and empty — wrap both pointers with modulo. Check: how do you tell full from empty?
c11_cs_cbse_10_014: A single-server line is plain FIFO — priorities belong to the event list, not the waiting line. Check: which queue is which?
c11_cs_cbse_11_001: A lab LAN is a network even with no internet — the internet is a network of networks. Check: does it need Google to count?
c11_cs_cbse_11_002: Wi-Fi across a campus is still a LAN — type follows geography, not cables or speed. Check: how far does it reach?
c11_cs_cbse_11_003: The star's centre is a switch, not a server — a server failing doesn't kill the network. Check: which device forwards frames?
c11_cs_cbse_11_004: A switch speaks MAC, not IP — it can't reach the internet alone. Check: which device routes?
c11_cs_cbse_11_005: Wi-Fi's headline speed is shared among all users — a wired port keeps its own lane. Check: shared or dedicated?
c11_cs_cbse_11_006: IPv6 groups are 16-bit hex chunks, not octets — and :: compresses zeros. Check: how many bits per group?
c11_cs_cbse_11_007: Most DNS answers come from cache — the root servers aren't queried every time. Check: what's the TTL doing?
c11_cs_cbse_11_008: Client and server are roles, not machines — your laptop can run both at once. Check: which process is asking?
c11_cs_cbse_11_009: HTTPS is just HTTP inside a TLS tunnel — and FTP passwords travel in plain text. Check: is anything encrypted?
c11_cs_cbse_11_010: Deleting a post doesn't erase it — backups, caches and screenshots keep it alive. Check: who else has a copy?
c11_cs_cbse_11_011: A Trojan isn't a virus — it pretends to be legit software and doesn't self-copy. Check: does it replicate?
c11_cs_cbse_11_012: Phishing isn't only obvious email scams — it can cite your real project details. Check: is it personalised?
c11_cs_cbse_11_013: Firewall filters traffic, antivirus scans files — one can't cover the other's gap. Check: packets or payloads?
c11_cs_cbse_11_014: Incognito only spares your local history — your ISP and the site still see you. Check: who's still watching?
c11_cs_cbse_11_015: Delete removes it from view — copies in backups and forwards still exist. Check: is it gone from servers?
c11_eco_cbse_01_001: Deindustrialisation wasn't 'no industry' — handicrafts died while a lopsided modern sector grew. Check: which sector grew?
c11_eco_cbse_01_002: The railways were real — but built for extraction, not development. Check: ports-to-mines or cities-to-cities?
c11_eco_cbse_01_003: Output did grow — it was yield per hectare and food per person that stagnated. Check: total or per hectare?
c11_eco_cbse_01_004: Ryotwari wasn't pro-peasant — the state's revenue demand could exceed a zamindar's. Check: what share was taken?
c11_eco_cbse_01_005: Farmers didn't choose cash crops — rigid cash revenue demands forced them. Check: voluntary or coerced?
c11_eco_cbse_01_006: Indian textiles weren't outcompeted — asymmetric tariffs and policy did the killing. Check: market or policy?
c11_eco_cbse_01_007: One steel plant isn't a capital-goods sector — TISCO made rails, not machine tools. Check: could it build machines?
c11_eco_cbse_01_008: The export surplus never reached India — it was claimed in London for home charges. Check: where did the sterling go?
c11_eco_cbse_01_009: The drain wasn't gold bullion leaving — it was goods and services paid with your own surplus. Check: what actually moved?
c11_eco_cbse_01_010: Tropical climate didn't kill — extraction, famine policy and 0.3% health spending did. Check: what did the state spend?
c11_eco_cbse_01_011: 72% of workers made only ~50% of GDP — agriculture hid mass underemployment. Check: workers' share or output's?
c11_eco_cbse_01_012: The network was real but rigged — guaranteed British returns paid from Indian revenues. Check: who got the returns?
c11_eco_cbse_02_001: The four goals weren't pursued equally — each plan picked a priority. Check: which goal led the Second Plan?
c11_eco_cbse_02_002: Agriculture-first was strategy, not backwardness — and abolishing intermediaries worked where ceilings didn't. Check: which reform failed?
c11_eco_cbse_02_003: The model didn't ignore agriculture — it assumed reforms that never came. Check: model flaw or execution gap?
c11_eco_cbse_02_004: The laws weren't weak on paper — courts, delays and benami transfers gutted them. Check: who kept the records?
c11_eco_cbse_02_005: HYV seeds aren't magic — they only out-yield with water and fertiliser. Check: what inputs came with the seed?
c11_eco_cbse_02_006: The Green Revolution didn't only help the rich — state credit and subsidies pulled small farmers in. Check: what's the counterfactual?
c11_eco_cbse_02_007: The private sector wasn't banned from heavy industry — Schedules B and C left it room. Check: ban or licence?
c11_eco_cbse_02_008: 'Small scale' is an investment ceiling, not headcount — that's what forces labour-intensive methods. Check: what's the criterion?
c11_eco_cbse_02_009: Imports weren't banned — tariffs made them pricey and quotas capped them. Check: autarky or protection?
c11_eco_cbse_02_010: Protection wasn't the sin — making it permanent and unconditional was. Check: was there a sunset clause?
c11_eco_cbse_02_011: The 'Hindu rate' wasn't the failure — 65% still in agriculture in 1990 was. Check: growth rate or structure?
c11_eco_cbse_03_001: Devaluation didn't cause the crisis — reserves had already collapsed. Check: which came first?
c11_eco_cbse_03_002: Letting a private firm enter is liberalisation; selling VSNL is privatisation. Check: new entry or asset sale?
c11_eco_cbse_03_003: Deregulation wasn't freedom — licences gave way to clearances and norms. Check: which approvals still apply?
c11_eco_cbse_03_004: The RBI didn't step back — it swapped quantity controls for prudential norms. Check: direct or indirect regulation?
c11_eco_cbse_03_005: Lower rates can mean more revenue — evasion shrinks; and GST unifies goods and services. Check: new name or new structure?
c11_eco_cbse_03_006: 1991 inflation was already running hot — devaluation added a nudge, not the fire. Check: what was WPI before?
c11_eco_cbse_03_007: Selling 5-10% keeps control — and Maharatna status isn't privatisation. Check: who still owns 51%?
c11_eco_cbse_03_008: The WTO caps tariffs, it doesn't zero them — and India keeps special flexibilities. Check: bound or applied rate?
c11_eco_cbse_03_009: 100% FDI isn't everywhere — caps and approval routes remain, and FII moves separately. Check: which sector's cap?
c11_eco_cbse_03_010: High growth doesn't prove fair shares — services can boom while 42% of workers crawl. Check: growth or distribution?
c11_eco_cbse_03_011: Free palm-oil imports hurt oilseeds while foreign barriers stayed — globalisation wasn't symmetric. Check: who kept their barriers?
c11_eco_cbse_04_001: A doctor isn't human capital — the skills embodied in them are; spending is just the flow. Check: stock or flow?
c11_eco_cbse_04_002: Human capital isn't just a degree — health, on-job training and even migration invest in it. Check: who else invests?
c11_eco_cbse_04_003: Education and growth feed each other — the arrow runs both ways. Check: cause or correlation?
c11_eco_cbse_04_004: More schooling doesn't mechanically grow GDP — quality and reverse causality muddy it. Check: private or social return?
c11_eco_cbse_04_005: Vaccination protects the herd, not just the child — health spend is investment, not welfare. Check: who else benefits?
c11_eco_cbse_04_006: On-the-job training costs downtime and trainer time — firms fund only firm-specific skills. Check: who pays for general skills?
c11_eco_cbse_04_007: RTE covers ages 6-14 and waives tuition — uniforms and foregone wages still cost. Check: free or fee-free?
c11_eco_cbse_04_008: Health spending isn't just hospitals — most of it is out-of-pocket outpatient care. Check: insurance or universal coverage?
c11_eco_cbse_04_009: Literacy counts readers, not skills — enrolment can rise while learning falls. Check: quantity or quality?
c11_eco_cbse_04_010: More hospitals doesn't mean healthier — prevention and the private-sector load matter more. Check: buildings or outcomes?
c11_eco_cbse_04_011: A higher literacy rate can hide falling learning — check outcomes, not enrolment. Check: what can a Class 5 child read?
c11_eco_cbse_05_001: Rural development isn't only farming — it's the non-farm linkages and credit adequacy too. Check: access or adequacy?
c11_eco_cbse_05_002: More branches didn't fix credit — collateral and loan-size economics still filter out small borrowers. Check: who can't pledge land?
c11_eco_cbse_05_003: High overdues aren't proof farmers won't repay — old stock can hide good current recovery. Check: stock or flow?
c11_eco_cbse_05_004: RRBs aren't mini commercial banks — they have their own Act, owners and a rural-only mandate. Check: who owns the shares?
c11_eco_cbse_05_005: SHGs aren't cheap-money clubs — members pay 2-3% a month, well above bank rates. Check: what's the internal rate?
c11_eco_cbse_05_006: Diversification isn't more crops — it's moving labour to allied and non-farm work. Check: crops or livelihoods?
c11_eco_cbse_05_007: Livestock isn't standalone — crop residues feed it and manure feeds the crops. Check: what feeds the animals?
c11_eco_cbse_05_008: Skipping chemicals isn't organic — it's a system of rotations and soil building. Check: is it certified practice?
c11_eco_cbse_05_009: Operation Flood's genius was the cooperative — not just better cows. Check: what guaranteed the price?
c11_eco_cbse_05_010: Big budgets aren't success — check who actually benefited and what asset got built. Check: outreach or outcome?
c11_eco_cbse_05_011: The Golden Revolution wasn't 'more fruit' — perishables need cold chains and new markets. Check: storable or perishable?
c11_eco_cbse_06_001: A solo cobbler is self-employed; a per-project coder may be casual labour. Check: who bears the risk?
c11_eco_cbse_06_002: Labour force includes the job-seekers — workforce is only those with work. Check: seeking or working?
c11_eco_cbse_06_003: Moving from farm to street-vending is a sector shift — not necessarily a pay rise. Check: share or income?
c11_eco_cbse_06_004: The primary share fell while farm headcount barely did — the rest of the economy grew faster. Check: share or level?
c11_eco_cbse_06_005: Informal isn't illegal — a registered 5-worker shop still counts as informal. Check: hired workers under 10?
c11_eco_cbse_06_006: Legality isn't the test — under 10 hired workers keeps you informal. Check: how many hired?
c11_eco_cbse_06_007: Not all unemployment is cyclical — a weaver's dead skill is involuntary, not a choice. Check: demand or skill mismatch?
c11_eco_cbse_06_008: There's no single unemployment rate — usual, weekly and daily status disagree by points. Check: which measure?
c11_eco_cbse_06_009: A rich solo consultant is informal; a government peon is formal. Check: what's the enterprise size?
c11_eco_cbse_06_010: MGNREGA isn't a cash transfer — wages buy person-days that must build assets. Check: what asset was created?
c11_eco_cbse_06_011: A job isn't automatically a good job — check wages, security and skill growth. Check: headcount or quality?
c11_eco_cbse_07_001: Renewable isn't limitless — pump faster than recharge and it's effectively gone. Check: extraction vs renewal rate?
c11_eco_cbse_07_002: It's not just headcount — livestock density and vehicle fleets degrade land differently. Check: whose footprint?
c11_eco_cbse_07_003: The water under your land isn't private — your pumping drops your neighbour's table too. Check: rival and excludable?
c11_eco_cbse_07_004: Smog isn't only a winter story — PM2.5 breaks limits year-round and ozone peaks in summer. Check: which pollutant, which season?
c11_eco_cbse_07_005: Poverty isn't the main polluter — the top 10%'s footprint dwarfs the bottom half's. Check: visible or aggregate impact?
c11_eco_cbse_07_006: It's not the poor felling forests — mining, dams and highways diverted 70% of forest land. Check: subsistence or projects?
c11_eco_cbse_07_007: Pollution's bill isn't just hospital charges — lost work, purifiers and future harm count too. Check: treatment or prevention cost?
c11_eco_cbse_07_008: Sustainable development isn't just 'green' — it's meeting today's needs without robbing tomorrow. Check: whose capital stock shrinks?
c11_eco_cbse_07_009: Daly doesn't ban non-renewables — deplete them only if renewable substitutes appear faster. Check: what replaced what?
c11_eco_cbse_07_010: These policies aren't just tree-planting — they price in social costs the market ignores. Check: which externality is internalised?
c11_eco_cbse_07_011: The ozone hole didn't cause warming — CFCs did both jobs separately. Check: ozone or climate mechanism?
c11_eco_cbse_08_001: China's boom drew on pre-1978 health and education — and a faster rate isn't a higher level. Check: base or flow?
c11_eco_cbse_08_002: The three reform packages weren't the same — China's was gradual and voluntary, India's crisis-forced. Check: who drove it?
c11_eco_cbse_08_003: Fertility at 2.0 doesn't stop growth — a young age structure keeps adding millions. Check: momentum or rate?
c11_eco_cbse_08_004: A shrinking population isn't automatically good news — watch the dependency ratio. Check: which stage of transition?
c11_eco_cbse_08_005: 6.5% on a small base can add less than 5% on a huge one — check absolute gains. Check: level or rate?
c11_eco_cbse_08_006: A rising services share isn't development if industry never absorbs the farm workforce. Check: where did the workers go?
c11_eco_cbse_08_007: China's HDI lead was banked before the reforms — stock, not current policy. Check: flow or accumulated stock?
c11_eco_cbse_08_008: Growth didn't buy China's health gains — the gains came first and enabled growth. Check: which way does the arrow run?
c11_eco_cbse_08_009: The Great Leap was forced collectivisation; 1978 was incentive redesign — and land stayed state-owned. Check: who owned the land?
c11_eco_cbse_08_010: Pakistan's 1988 reforms were narrow — denationalisation without trade or tax deepening. Check: comprehensive or partial?
c11_eco_cbse_08_011: India started 13 years late and crisis-forced — comparisons ignore China's head start. Check: voluntary or forced?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_001: The grandmother's beliefs aren't quirks — they carry a whole generation's worldview. Check: personal quirk or cultural frame?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_002: The story isn't a straight timeline — an adult narrator looks back through three emotional phases. Check: who's telling it, and when?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_003: Setting is the where; atmosphere is the feeling it builds — the motor bus carries alienation. Check: which detail makes the mood?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_004: She isn't passive tradition — feeding sparrows and drumming were her choices. Check: what did she choose?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_005: 'Minor' characters aren't filler — the priest and the sparrows frame her world. Check: what contrast do they draw?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_006: It isn't about the gap — it's how dignity and prayer bridged it. Check: guilt or grace?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_007: A theme is an abstract idea — 'growing apart', not 'he went to university'. Check: event or idea?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_008: Not every adjective is imagery — ask which sense it fires. Check: which sense does it touch?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_009: One mention doesn't make a symbol — the spinning wheel recurs; the bus doesn't. Check: does it carry the theme?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_010: Context is bigger than the sentence — the grandmother's character colours 'serenity'. Check: denotation or connotation?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_011: Past perfect orders two past events — it isn't just a fancier past tense. Check: which event came first?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_012: A long answer can still be literal — inferential means reasoning past the text. Check: is it stated or implied?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_013: Listing themes isn't analysis — trace how her silence and song exert agency. Check: what does the structure argue?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_014: Don't retell the story — pick the details that answer the prompt. Check: what is the question asking?
c11_eng_h_cbse_01_015: A good discussion argues from the text — 'the sparrows' silence is an elegy' beats 'I felt sad'. Check: claim or anecdote?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_001: The 1976 date mirrors Cook's 1768 — the parallel is the point, not trivia. Check: why Plymouth in July?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_002: The climax is the wave strike itself — the 15-hour struggle is falling action. Check: where does tension peak?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_003: The ocean's mood isn't fixed — each scene selects different details to build it. Check: which details changed?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_004: He's no invincible hero — the text shows him smashed, blacking out, dozing off. Check: where does he falter?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_005: Mary and Larry aren't plot tools — cheerfulness under stress is the point. Check: what trait keeps them going?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_006: 'Survival' is a topic — the theme is what the story says about it. Check: what insight does it offer?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_007: Sue's injury isn't a theme — the selfless protection it shows is. Check: event or idea?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_008: 'Chewing the hull' is an implied metaphor — the sea-as-enemy mapping runs through the text. Check: which sense is evoked?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_009: Bad luck isn't irony — the fearless title worn by frightened adults is. Check: expectation vs outcome?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_010: Don't grab the first dictionary sense — gather the sentence's clues; 'honing' implies years of practice. Check: what evidence clusters?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_011: In 'flagship' the ship is a vessel, not a state — same spelling, different morpheme. Check: suffix or compound?
c11_eng_h_cbse_02_012: Inference isn't free opinion — anchor each claim to a textual clue. Check: which line proves it?
